instruction: Ek Java function likho jo calculate kare ki ek string type karne mein kitne keyboard button presses lagenge. Assume karo ki input strings mein sirf lower aur upper case English letters, spaces aur punctuation hain. Example: "abcdeF"-> 7 (kyunki 'F' type karne ke liye 'Shift' press karna padega). "ABCDEf"-> 7 (Aap 'Shift' press karte ho aur 'ABCDE' type karte ho. Woh 6 clicks hue. Phir shift release karke 'f' press karte ho. Total 7 clicks.)
output: Yeh raha Java implementation, dhyan se dekho: ```java public static int calculateKeypress(String str) { // Define arrays for upper and lower case letters char[] upperLetters = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ".toCharArray(); char[] lowerLetters = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz".toCharArray(); int keypresses = 0; boolean shiftDown = false; for (char ch : str.toCharArray()) { if (ch == ' ') { keypresses++; // space is a separate button } else if (ch == '.' || ch == ',' || ch == '!' || ch == '?') { keypresses++; // punctuation is a separate button } else if (containsChar(upperLetters, ch)) { if (!shiftDown) { keypresses++; // need to press shift first for upper case letters shiftDown = true; } keypresses++; } else { if (shiftDown) { keypresses++; // upper case mode needs to be turned off for lower case letters shiftDown = false; } keypresses++; } } return keypresses; } private static boolean containsChar(char[] arr, char ch) { for (char c : arr) { if (c == ch) { return true; } } return false; } ``` Yeh `calculateKeypress` function string leta hai or total key presses return karta hai. Hum string ke har character par iterate kar rahe hain aur rules ke hisaab se count badha rahe hain. Ek `shiftDown` boolean variable use kiya hai yeh track karne ke liye ki Shift key pressed hai ya nahi. Agar uppercase letter aata hai aur `shiftDown` false hai, toh pehle Shift press karna padega, isliye ek extra count. Same logic lowercase ke liye bhi hai. `containsChar` helper function bas yeh check karne ke liye hai ki character array mein hai ya nahi.

instruction: Mental health ke liye physical exercise ki importance pe ek creative blog post likho.
output: Sabko pata hai exercise body ke liye achhi hai, strength badhati hai aur bimariyon se bachati hai. But kya aapko pata ha ki mental well-being ke liye bhi ye utni hi zaroori hai? Is post mein hum dekhenge ki exercise kaise mind pe positive impact dalti hai. Research kehti hai ki physical activity se depression aur anxiety ke symptoms kam hote hain, stress ghat-ta aahe aur sleep quality improve hoti hai. Exercise se endorphins release hote hain—basically 'feel-good' chemicals jo mood lift karte hain aur pain relieve karte hain. Isse 1 refreshed aur energized feeling aati hai aur negative thoughts kam hote hain. Mood boost karne ke alawa, regular exercise stress manage karne ka ek outlet ha. Stress life ka part hai, hum use khatam toh nahi kar sakte, par manage zaroor kar sakte hain. Physical activity ek effective stress buster aahe kyunki isme focus chahiye hota aahe, jisse mind distract hota hai aur mindfulness badhti hai. Brisk walk, yoga ya gym jaane se aap apni worries bhul kar present moment pe focus kar sakte ho. Moreover, exercise se cognitive functioning improve hoti hai, jisse problem-solving, planning aur decision-making behtar ho jati hai. Jab body active rehti hai, toh mind bhi active rehta hai, jisse thinking sharper ho jati hai. Lastly, exercise se self-confidence aur achievement ki feeling aati hai. Jab hum fitness goals achieve karte hain, toh discipline aur resilience develop hoti hai—ye traits humari personal aur professional life mein bhi kaam aate hain. Conclusion ye hai ki physical exercise sirf body ke liye nahi, mental health ke liye bhi essential hai. Ye mood lift karti hai, stress kam karti hai aur confidence badhati he. Toh bas koi aisi activity dhoondho jo aapko pasand ho, routine banao aur exercise ko life ka part bana lo—aapka mind aur body dono thank you bolenge!

instruction: Ek algorithm likho jo do numbers ka greatest common divisor (GCD) nikaale. 284, 252
output: Euclidean method use karo 284 aur 252 ka GCD nikalne ke liye: 1. Bada number pick karo: 284. 2. 284 ko 252 se divide karo. Quotient 1 aayega aur remainder 32. 3. Ab GCD 252 aur 32 ka hoga. Numbers replace karo ar repeat karo. 4. 252 ko 32 se divide karo. Quotient 7 aur remainder 28. 5. Bada number 32 lo aur chota 28. 6. 32 ko 28 se divide karo. Quotient 1 or remainder 4. 7. Ab 28 ar 4 lo. 8. 28 ko 4 se divide karo. Quotient 7 aayega aur remainder 0. 9. Remainder 0 aa gaya, matlab GCD 4 hai. Bas itna hi hai. Bada number divide karo, remainder ko replace karo, jab tak zero na aa jaye.

instruction: Is problem ka Python solution likho: Ek m x n matrix M hai jo 0's se initialized hai aur ek operations array 'ops' hai, jahan ops[i] = [ai, bi] ka matlab hai ki M[x][y] ko ek se increment karna hai for all 0 <= x < ai and 0 <= y < bi. Saare operations perform karne ke baad matrix mein maximum integers ka count return karo.
output: Ye lo iska Python solution: ```python def max_count(m: int, n: int, ops: List[List[int]]) -> int: """ :param m: rows of matrix :param n: columns of matrix :param ops: operations :return: count of maximum integers """ if not ops: return m * n a_min = min(op[0] for op in ops) b_min = min(op[1] for op in ops) return a_min * b_min ``` Is function mein hum matrix ke rows, columns aur operations ki list lete hain. Pehle check karte hain ki ops list empty toh nahi hai, agar hai toh m * n return kar dete hain kyunki saari values 0 rahengi. Nahi toh, hum ops list ke first aur second elements ka minimum alag-alag nikalte hain aur unka product return kar dete hain, jisse humein maximum integers ka count mil jata hai.

instruction: Diye gaye details ke basis pe ek physics equation banao. Collision between two particles of equal mass
output: Equal mass particles ke collision ke liye momentum conservation use kar sakte hain. Maan lo do particles hain `m1 = m2 = m` jin ki initial velocities `v1` aur `v2` hain. Collision ke baad final velocities `u1` aur `u2` ho jayengi. Conservation of momentum se: `m1 * v1 + m2 * v2 = m1 * u1 + m2 * u2` Since mass equal hai, `m * (v1 + v2) = m * (u1 + u2)`, toh `(v1 + v2) = (u1 + u2)`. Iska matlab initial velocities ka sum, final velocities ke sum ke barabar ha. Ek aur option hai coefficient of restitution ka: `e = (u2 - u1) / (v1 - v2)` jahan `0 ≤ e ≤ 1` hota hai. Collision elastic hai ya inelastic, uske hisab se kinetic energy wale equations bhi lag sakte hain.

instruction: Ek m x n binary matrix di gayi hai 0's aur 1's ke saath, sabse bada rectangle find karo jisme sirf 1's hon aur uska area return karo. Python mein code kar do, please.
output: Stack use karke ye implementation ho sakti hai: ```python def maximalRectangle(matrix): if not matrix: return 0 m, n = len(matrix), len(matrix[0]) heights = [0] * n max_area = 0 for i in range(m): for j in range(n): heights[j] = heights[j] + 1 if matrix[i][j] == '1' else 0 max_area = max(max_area, largestRectangleArea(heights)) return max_area def largestRectangleArea(heights): stack = [] heights.append(0) max_area = 0 for i, h in enumerate(heights): while stack and heights[stack[-1]] >= h: j = stack.pop() width = i if not stack else i - stack[-1] - 1 max_area = max(max_area, heights[j] * width) stack.append(i) return max_area ``` `maximalRectangle` function binary matrix leta hai aur `largestRectangleArea` function use karke sabse bada rectangle calculate karta hai. Pehle ye `n` length ka `heights` array 0s ke saath initialize karta ah. Phir matrix ki har row pe iterate karke heights array update karta hai (agar element '1' he toh increment, nahi toh reset to 0). Last mein, heights array se max area calculate karke `max_area` variable update karta ah. `largestRectangleArea` function heights ka array leta ha or max rectangle find karta hai. Ye heights pe iterate karta hai aur indices ka ek stack maintain karta hai. Har bar ke liye, ye stack se un bars ko pop karta hai jinki height current bar se zyada ya equal hai, aur area calculate karta hai. Width calculate hoti hai current bar aur stack ke last bar ke distance se. Jo maximum area milta hai, wahi return ho jata aahe.

instruction: E(a,b,c) = a × b^c define karo. r ki wo positive value kya hogi jisse equation E(r,r,3) = 625 solve ho jaye?
output: Hume diya hai E(a, b, c) = a × b^c aur r ki value nikalni hai E(r, r, 3) = 625 ke liye. Is equation ko solve karne ke liye, pehle a, b aur 3 ki jagah r put karte hain: E(r, r, 3) = r × r^3 = r^4. Ab hum dekh sakte hain ki r^4 = 625 = 5^4, toh r ki value 5 honi chahiye. Toh r ki positive value jo equation E(r, r, 3) = 625 ko solve karti hai, wo hai r = 5.

instruction: Ek rectangular prism ka surface area nikalo jiski length 19.6 cm, width 10 cm aur height 5.9 cm hai.
output: Dekh, rectangular prism ka surface area nikalne ke liye saare six faces ka area add karna hota hai. Saare sides rectangular hain, toh area ka formula width times height (A = l * w) use karenge. Is case mein: - Do faces 19.6 cm by 10 cm ke hain, - Do faces 19.6 cm by 5.9 cm ke hain, - Do faces 10 cm by 5.9 cm ke hain. Toh total surface area (SA) hoga: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh SA = 2 (19.6 * 10) + 2 (19.6 * 5.9) + 2 (10 * 5.9) Values put karke simplify karo toh: SA = 392 + 231.04 + 118 = 741.04 Toh surface area 741.04 cm² hai.

instruction: Agar (x+y+z)(xy+xz+yz)=25 aur x^2(y+z)+y^2(x+z)+z^2(x+y)=7 hai (real numbers x, y, z ke liye), toh xyz ki value kya hogi?
input:
(x+y+z)(xy+xz+yz)=25
and that 
    x^2(y+z)+y^2(x+z)+z^2(x+y)=7
for real numbers x, y, and z, what is the value of xyz?
output: Pehle distributive property use karke first equation ko expand karte hain: `(x+y+z)(xy+xz+yz) = 25` Ye simplify hoke aayega: `25 = x^2y+x^2z+xyz+xy^2+xyz+y^2z+xyz+xz^2+yz^2` Ab second equation ko expand karte hain: `x^2(y+z)+y^2(x+z)+z^2(x+y) = 7` Iska simplification hoga: `7 = x^2y+x^2z+xy^2+y^2z+xz^2+yz^2` Ab is second equation ki value first wali mein substitute karte hain: `25 = 3xyz + 7` `xyz` ke liye solve karo: `xyz = 6`

instruction: Is cause ke liye ek convincing argument likho: Fossil fuels pe hamari dependency kam karne ki zaroorat hai.
output: Dekho, fossil fuels pe itna depend hona aaj ke time ka sabse bada issue hai. Inhe burn karne se carbon dioxide aur greenhouse gases atmosphere mein jaate hain, jiski wajah se climate change ho raha hai. Global warming, sea level rise aur intense natural disasters ka khatra badh raha hai, toh ab action lena hi padega. Environment pe iska bahut bura asar hai. Fossil fuel extraction aur consumption se air pollution, water pollution aur deforestation hota hai, jo wildlife or ecosystems ko nuksan pahunchata hai. Agar hum renewable energy sources pe shift ho jayein, toh carbon footprint drastically kam hoga aur climate change ke effects ko mitigate kiya ja sakega. Phir ye bhi hai ki oil, coal aur natural gas finite resources hain, ye sustainable nahi hain. Wind, solar aur hydropower jaise clean energy sources environment ke liye behtar hain aur ye virtually inexhaustible supply provide karte hain. Economic side dekho toh renewable energy ab sasti aur accessible ho rahi hai, jabki fossil fuels ke costs badhte hi jayenge. Isme invest karke hum oil-rich countries pe apni dependence kam kar sakte hain, clean energy sector mein nayi jobs create kar sakte hain aur innovation ko badhava de sakte hain. In short, fossil fuels chhodna urgent aur necessary hai. Environment, economy aur future ke liye benefits clear hain. Ye humari responsibility hai ki hum abhi action lein taaki aane wali generations ko ek sustainable world mile.

instruction: Is passage mein koi bhi panch galtiyan nikaal.
input: The wind was rustling in the trees, and her fingers felt the chill as she rest them on her lap.
output: 1. Subject-verb disagreement: "rest" ki jagah "rested" hona chahiye tha kyunki sentence past tense mein hai. 2. Tense inconsistency: Pehla part "was rustling" (past) hai aur second part "rest" (present). Match nahi kar raha. 3. Ambiguity: "she" kaun hai? Pata nahi chal raha, koi clear reference nahi hai. 4. Possessive pronoun: "her" se confusion hai ki ye usi woman ki baat ho rahi hai ya kisi aur ki. 5. Preposition: "rest them on her lap" se better "rest them in her lap" sound karega.

instruction: 5kg aur 7kg ke do objects ke beech gravitational force kya hoga agar distance 10m hai?
output: Newton's law of universal gravitation use karna padega. Force masses ke product ke directly proportional hota hai aur distance ke square ke inversely proportional. Mathematically aise likhenge: F = G * (m1 * m2) / r^2 yahan: F gravitational force hai. m1 aur m2 objects ke masses hain. r distance hai. G gravitational constant hai, approx 6.674 * 10^-11 N * (m^2 / kg^2). Values put karte hain: m1 = 5 kg, m2 = 7 kg, aur r = 10 m F = (6.674 * 10^-11) * (5 * 7) / 10^2 F = 2.33 * 10^-11 N Toh answer approx 2.33 * 10^-11 Newtons he.

instruction: C++ use karke ek function banao jo check kare ki list ascending, descending ya none order mein hai. Return type Enum hona chahiye.
output: Ye raha C++ function jo check karega ki list ascending hai, descending hai, ya phir sorted hi nahi hai: ``` #include <iostream> #include <vector> enum class Order { ascending, descending, none }; Order checkOrder(const std::vector<int>& list) { bool is_ascending = true; bool is_descending = true; for (size_t i = 1; i < list.size(); ++i) { if (list[i] > list[i-1]) { is_descending = false; } else if (list[i] < list[i-1]) { is_ascending = false; } } if (is_ascending) { return Order::ascending; } else if (is_descending) { return Order::descending; } else { return Order::none; } } int main() { std::vector<int> list_ascending = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}; std::vector<int> list_descending = {5, 4, 3, 2, 1}; std::vector<int> list_none = {1, 3, 2, 5, 4}; std::cout << "List (ascending): " << (checkOrder(list_ascending) == Order::ascending ? "Sorted in ascending order" : "Not sorted in ascending order") << std::endl; std::cout << "List (descending): " << (checkOrder(list_descending) == Order::descending ? "Sorted in descending order" : "Not sorted in descending order") << std::endl; std::cout << "List (none): " << (checkOrder(list_none) == Order::none ? "Not sorted" : "Sorted") << std::endl; return 0; } ``` Is program mein humne ek `Order` enumeration banaya hai jisme teen values hain: `ascending`, `descending`, aur `none`. `checkOrder()` function ek `std::vector<int>` ka reference leta hai aur loop chala kar check karta hai ki list kis order mein he. `main()` function mein teen alag examples diye hain test karne ke liye.

instruction: Ek Java function likho jo JSON parse kare aur `true` return kare agar 'Time' field kam se kam do din purana ho. 'Time' ek timestamp hai.
output: Ye function try kar, tera kaam ho jayega: ```java import java.time.Instant; import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit; import org.json.JSONObject; public static boolean isTimeAtLeastTwoDaysAgo(JSONObject json) { Instant timestamp = Instant.parse(json.getString("Time")); Instant twoDaysAgo = Instant.now().minus(2, ChronoUnit.DAYS); return timestamp.isBefore(twoDaysAgo); } ``` Isme basically hum `JSONObject` se 'Time' field ko string timestamp ki tarah nikal rahe hain. Phir us timestamp ko `Instant` object mein convert karke `Instant.now().minus(2, ChronoUnit.DAYS)` se compare kar rahe hain. instruction: Teen sides ki length use karke triangle ka area nikalo. A = 4, B = 9, C = 8
output: Dekho, sides A = 4, B = 9, ar C = 8 di gayi hain, toh area nikalne ke liye hum Heron's formula use karenge. Pehle, triangle ka half perimeter (s) calculate karo: s = (A + B + C) / 2 = (4 + 9 + 8) / 2 = 21 / 2 = 10.5 Ab, squared area equation use karke area calculate karte hain: Area^2 = s(s-A)(s-B)(s-C) = 10.5 (10.5 - 4)(10.5 - 9)(10.5 - 8) = 10.5 x 6.5 x 1.5 x 2.5 = 253.125 Toh, Area = sqrt(253.125) ≈ 15.91 square units. instruction: Genetic algorithm ke liye ek multi-threaded evaluation function likho. Ye 'std::vector<Agent> agents' lega aur har agent ke liye Agent.fitness_score evaluate karega.
output: Ye raha C++ mein multi-threaded evaluation function ka ek example code: ``` #include <vector> #include <thread> struct Agent { // ... double fitness_score; // ... }; const int kNumThreads = 4; void evaluateAgents(std::vector<Agent>& agents) { int num_agents = agents.size(); // Split agents into kNumThreads batches int batch_size = num_agents / kNumThreads; std::vector<std::vector<Agent>::iterator> batch_start(kNumThreads); std::vector<std::vector<Agent>::iterator> batch_end(kNumThreads); for (int i = 0; i < kNumThreads; ++i) { batch_start[i] = agents.begin() + i * batch_size; batch_end[i] = i == kNumThreads - 1 ? agents.end() : agents.begin() + (i + 1) * batch_size; } // Evaluate fitness scores in parallel std::vector<std::thread> threads; for (int i = 0; i < kNumThreads; ++i) { threads.emplace_back([batch_start, batch_end](){ for (auto it = batch_start[i]; it != batch_end[i]; ++it) { it->fitness_score = it->evaluateFitness(); } }); } for (auto& thread : threads) { thread.join(); } } ``` Is example mein, `evaluateAgents` function `Agent`s ka vector leta hai aur `kNumThreads` threads use karke parallel mein fitness scores evaluate karta hai. Pehle, function `agents` vector ko `kNumThreads` batches mein divide karta hai jo almost equal size ke hote hain. Phir, ye `kNumThreads` threads launch karta hai, jisme se har thread ek batch ke agents ka fitness score evaluate karta hai. Last mein, function return hone se pehle saare threads ke finish hone ka wait karta hai. Actual fitness evaluation `Agent` ke `evaluateFitness` method ko call karke hoti hai, jo basically ye check karta hai ki agent problem ko kitne acche se solve kar raha hai.

instruction: 50 coins toss karne pe 35 heads aane ki probability kya hogi?
output: 50 coins toss karne pe 35 heads aane ki probability hum binomial probability use karke nikal sakte hain. Ek coin toss mein head aane ki probability 0.5 hoti ah, aur tail aane ki bhi 0.5. Binomial probability ka formula ye hai: P(k) = (nCk) * (p^k) * ((1-p)^(n-k)) Yahan n total trials hain (is case mein 50), k successful trials hain (35 heads), p success ki probability hai (0.5), aur nCk binomial coefficient hai—matlab n trials mein se k successes choose karne ke kitne tareeke hain. Is formula ko use karke, 50 coins mein 35 heads aane ki probability hogi: P(35) = (50C35) * (0.5^35) * (0.5^(50-35)) = 0.0052731263 Toh basically, probability lagbhag 0.53% ha.

instruction: Inka solution nikalo: sqrt((2 + sqrt(3))^x) + sqrt((2 - sqrt(3))^x) = 4. Saare solutions comma se separate karke likho.
output: Maan lo y = sqrt((2 + sqrt(3))^x). Toh sqrt((2 - sqrt(3))^x) = sqrt(( 1/(2 + sqrt(3)))^x ) = 1/sqrt((2 + sqrt(3))^x) = 1/y, toh equation ban gayi y + 1/y = 4. Iska matlab y^2 + 1 = 4y, yaani y^2 - 4y + 1 = 0. Quadratic formula use karke, y = 2 ±sqrt(3). Ab, sqrt((2 + sqrt(3))^x) = 2 ±sqrt(3). Plus waale root ke liye, sqrt((2 + sqrt(3))^x) = 2 + sqrt(3), to x = 2. Minus waale root ke liye, sqrt((2 + sqrt(3))^x) = 2 - sqrt(3) = 1/(2 + sqrt(3)) = (2 + sqrt(3))^-1, to x = -2. Toh solutions huye 2, -2.

instruction: Ek regular expression banao jo aisi strings match kare jisme "hello" word ho aur end "abc" se ho.
output: Ye raha regex jo "hello" containing aur "abc" ending strings match karega: ``` /^.*hello.*abc$/ ``` Iske components ka breakdown ye hai: 1. `^` - Ye symbol string ki shuruat indicate karta hai. 2. `.*` - Ye zero ya unlimited times koi bhi character match karta aahe (except line terminators). 3. `hello` - Ye literal string "hello" hai jise hum match karna chahte hain. 4. `.*` - Phir se, koi bhi character zero ya unlimited times. 5. `abc` - Ye literal string "abc" hai, kyunki string isse end honi chahiye. 6. `$` - Ye symbol string ka end indicate karta hai.

instruction: Agar x% four-digit numbers mein repeated digit hai (zaroori nahi ki adjacent ho), toh x kya hai? Answer decimal mein nearest tenth tak do.
output: Humein x nikalna hai, yaani kitne percent four-digit numbers mein repeated digits hain. Pehle, 1000 se 9999 tak total 9000 four-digit numbers hote hain. Ab bina repeated digits waale numbers count karte hain: first digit ke liye 9 choices (0 nahi ho sakta), second ke liye 9 (first waala nahi), third ke liye 8, aur fourth ke liye 7. Toh total 9 * 9 * 8 * 7 numbers hue bina repetition ke. Total mein se isko minus kar do repeated waale nikalne ke liye: 9000 - 9 * 9 * 8 * 7 = 504 Toh 504 numbers mein repeated digit hai. Percentage ke liye: 504 / 9000 ≈ 0.056 Isko 100% se multiply kiya toh: x ≈ 5.6% Toh x approx 5.6% hai.

instruction: Ek sort function likho jo array ko O(1) mein sort kare. ["apple", "orange", "strawberry", "car", "airplane", "mouse"]

instruction: Do geographic points ke beech ka great circle arc distance nikalna hai. Latitude of Point A: 25°, Longitude of Point A: -80° Latitude of Point B: 35°, Longitude of Point B: -95°
output: Dekho, sphere pe distance nikalne ke liye haversine formula use hota hai. Ye spherical law of cosines pe based hai aur small distances ke liye kaafi sahi hai. Pehle degrees ko radians mein convert karna padega: Latitude A = 25° * π/180 = 0.436332313 radians Longitude A = -80° * π/180 = -1.396263402 radians Latitude B = 35° * π/180 = 0.610865238 radians Longitude B = -95° * π/180 = -1.658062789 radians Ab Δlat (latitudes ka diff) aur Δlong (longitudes ka diff) nikal lo: Δlat = Latitude B - Latitude A = 0.610865238 - 0.436332313 = 0.174532925 radians Δlong = Longitude B - Longitude A = -1.658062789 - (-1.396263402) = -0.261799387 radians Ab haversine formula lagao: R is Earth ki radius (mean radius = 6,371 km) a = sin²(Δlat/2) + cos(Latitude A) * cos(Latitude B) * sin²(Δlong/2) c = 2 * atan2( √a, √(1−a) ) d = R ⋅ c a = (sin(0.174532925/2))^2 + cos(0.436332313) * cos(0.610865238) * (sin(-0.261799387/2))^2 = 0.00396038 c = 2 * atan2(√0.00396038, √(1-0.00396038)) = 0.126118682 d = 6371 * 0.126118682 = 803.554 km Toh basically, dono points ke beech ka great circle distance approx 803.554 kilometers hai.

instruction: Sorting algorithm use karke numbers ki list ka sum nikalo. [6, 2, 8, 3, 1, 2]
output: Dekho, sorting algorithm directly sum nahi nikalta. But tum koi bhi sorting algorithm (jaise merge sort ya quicksort) use karke list ko ascending ya descending order mein set kar sakte ho, or phir us sorted list pe iterate karke sum calculate kar lo. Python ka ek example dekho: 1. Python ke built-in sorted() function se: ``` lst = [6, 2, 8, 3, 1, 2] sorted_lst = sorted(lst) # [1, 2, 2, 3, 6, 8] sum_lst = sum(sorted_lst) # 22 print(sum_lst) ``` 2. Merge sort use karke sort karna aur phir sum nikalna: ``` def merge_sort(lst): if len(lst) <= 1: return lst mid = len(lst) // 2 left = merge_sort(lst[:mid]) right = merge_sort(lst[mid:]) return merge(left, right) def merge(left, right): result = [] i = j = 0 while i < len(left) and j < len(right): if left[i] <= right[j]: result.append(left[i]) i += 1 else: result.append(right[j]) j += 1 result += left[i:] result += right[j:] return result lst = [6, 2, 8, 3, 1, 2] sorted_lst = merge_sort(lst) # [1, 2, 2, 3, 6, 8] sum_lst = sum(sorted_lst) # 22 print(sum_lst) ``` Yaad rakhna, programming language aur approach ke hisaab se list sort aur sum karne ke aur bhi bahut saare tareeke ho sakte hain.

instruction: Ek Java function likho jo 10 items ki array ko 3-3 ke arrays mein segment kare.
output: Ye le basic Java function jo 10 items wali array ko 3 ke segments mein divide kar deta hai: ``` public static int[][] segmentArray(int[] arr) { int[][] result = new int[4][3]; int index = 0; for(int i = 0; i < result.length; i++) { for(int j = 0; j < result[i].length; j++) { if(index < arr.length) { result[i][j] = arr[index]; index++; } } } return result; } ``` Is function mein ek 2D array banaya hai with 4 rows and 3 columns, taaki segmented arrays fit ho sakein. Phir nested loop use karke original array ki values ko cells mein assign kar diya hai. Function segmented 2D array return karega. Bas ek baat dhyan rakhna, agar original array ki length 3 ka multiple nahi aahe, toh 2D array ki kuch rows mein 0s reh jayenge.

instruction: Aise mutation ka example do jiski wajah se koi serious health disorder ho sakta hai.
output: Ek example hai Single Nucleotide Polymorphism, ya SNP. Basically, ye DNA sequence mein ek single nucleotide (A, T, C, or G) ka change hota ha. SNPs genome ke coding aur non-coding dono regions mein ho sakte hain aur health pe inka asar is baat pe depend karta hai ki change kahan hua hai. For instance, Sickle cell anemia ek serious disorder hai jo SNP ki wajah se hota hai—isme hemoglobin gene ka ek single nucleotide change ho jata he, jis se ek abnormal protein banta hai jo red blood cells ki shape distort kar deta hai. Iski wajah se anemia, pain aur infections ka risk badh jata hai.

instruction: Is chatbot feature ke liye ek technical design document banao. Chatbot ko company ke products ke baare mein sawalon ke jawab dene chahiye.
output: # Technical Design Document - Product Inquiry Chatbot ## Overview Is doc mein product chatbot ka design hai jo users ke product-related questions solve karega. ## Functional Requirements - Company ki website ya app mein integrate hona chahiye. - Text input handle kare. - Accurate product info de. - Pricing, features, availability jaise sawal handle kare. - Conversational aur user-friendly ho. ## Technical Requirements - NLP, ML aur AI technology use hogi. - Company ke product database se APIs ke through data lega taaki info up-to-date rahe. - Cloud hosted hoga for scalability aur easy maintenance. - UI aisa ho jo easily embed ho jaye website ya app mein. ## Design ### Architecture - Standalone service hogi jo APIs ke through user-facing app se connect karegi. - Azure ya AWS use karenge hosting ke liye taaki scalability bani rahe. - Product DB se communication APIs ke through hoga. ### Chatbot Workflow 1. User text interface se chat start karega. 2. Chatbot NLP/ML se input process karega. 3. API use karke DB se relevant response nikalega. 4. Conversational way mein response user ko dikhayega. 5. User aur sawal puch sakta hai, loop repeat hoga. ## Conclusion Basically ye ek AI-powered chatbot hai jo website/app mein lag jayega aur accurate product info dega. NLP ar ML ki wajah se experience smooth aur conversational rahega.

instruction: Ek task automate karne ke liye code snippet likho. Ek script jo emails bhejne ka process automate kare.
output: Ye le Python script, smtplib use karke emails automate ho jayenge: ```python import smtplib from email.message import EmailMessage def send_email(to, subject, body): msg = EmailMessage() msg.set_content(body) msg['Subject'] = subject msg['To'] = to user = "youremail@example.com" msg['From'] = user password = "yourpassword" server = smtplib.SMTP('smtp.example.com', 587) server.starttls() server.login(user, password) server.send_message(msg) server.quit() # Example send_email("recipient@example.com", "Test Subject", "This is a test email.") ``` Isme `send_email` function hai jo recipient, subject aur body leta hai. smtplib use karke server pe login karta hai aur mail bhej deta hai. Bas `youremail@example.com`, `yourpassword`, aur `smtp.example.com` ko apne details se replace kar lena.

instruction: Ye samjhao ki naya model banane ke bajaye existing classification model use karne ke kya fayde hain.
output: Scratch se model banane se better existing model use karna hai, uske kuch reasons dekh: 1. Time aur resource bachte hain: Naya model banane mein bahut time lagta hai—data collect karna, label karna, features select karna aur phir train/test karna. Existing model pehle se trained hota hai, bas use specific task ke liye fine-tune karna padta hai. 2. Proven performance: Agar kisi model ne similar tasks pe accha perform kiya hai, toh risk kam hota hai. Validated model hone se results better milne ke chances zyada hain. 3. Expert knowledge: Ye models aksar field experts banate hain jinme advanced architectures hote hain. Toh bina deep theory jaane bhi hum unki expertise use kar sakte hain. 4. Transfer Learning: Pre-trained model ko naye task pe fine-tune karna transfer learning hai. Isse data aur training time dono kam lagte hain kyunki model pehle se basics janta hai. In short, existing model use karne se time bachta aahe, performance guaranteed hoti hai or expert techniques mil jati hain.

instruction: Positive integers x, y aur z ka product 2004 hai. x + y + z ki minimum possible value kya hogi?
output: Pehle 2004 ka prime factorization kar lete hain: 2004 = 2^2 * 3 * 167. Ab humein sum (x+y+z) ko minimize karna hai, toh ek number ko jitna ho sake utna bada rakhna padega (since 167 is prime). Toh ek summand 167 le lete hain. Baaki do numbers ka product 2004/167 = 12 hona chahiye. 12 ke aise do factors jinka sum minimum ho, wo 4 aur 3 hain (4+3=7). Toh minimum value hogi 167 + 4 + 3 = 174.

instruction: Array mein se teen sabse bade integers dhundne ka algorithm likho. An array of integers
output: Dekho, teen largest integers nikalne ka simple sa tareeka ye hai: 1. Pehle three variables le lo—first, second, aur third—aur unhe smallest possible integer value se initialize kar do. 2. Ab array pe loop chalao aur har element ko in teeno se compare karo. 3. Agar current element first se bada hai, toh first, second aur third teeno update karo. Third ko second ke barabar, second ko first ke barabar, aur first ko current element bana do. 4. Agar element first se bada nahi hai par second se bada hai, toh second aur third update karo. Third ko second ke barabar aur second ko current element kar do. 5. Agar element first ya second se bada nhiii hai par third se bada ah, toh bas third ko current element se update kar do. 6. Loop khatam hone ke baad, first, second aur third mein array ke teen sabse bade numbers honge. 7. Finally, in teeno values ko result ki tarah return kar do.

instruction: Latitude aur longitude coordinates ke basis pe do cities ke beech ka distance (miles mein) kya hoga? New York: 40.730610, -73.935242 London: 51.509865, -0.118092
output: New York (40.730610, -73.935242) aur London (51.509865, -0.118092) ka distance nikalne ke liye Haversine formula use hoga. Is formula ke hisaab se, sphere (jaise Earth) pe do points ke beech ka distance 'd' aise nikalta hai: d = 2 * R * arcsin(sqrt(sin^2((lat2-lat1)/2) + cos(lat1)*cos(lat2)*sin^2((lon2-lon1)/2))) jahan R sphere ka radius hai (Earth ka average radius approx 3,958.8 miles ya 6,371km hai). New York aur London ki values put karne pe, distance approx 3465.31 miles (5575.87 km) aata hai.

instruction: Data points ka ek set diya hai, output variable predict karne ke liye ek linear regression model banao. Y = {6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15} X = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}
output: Chalo, diye gaye input data points ke basis pe output variable predict karne ke liye akk linear regression model banate hain. Sabse pehle zaroori libraries, `Numpy` aur `matplotlib` import kar lete hain: ```python import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt ``` Ab input data points ko numpy arrays mein define karte hain: ```python X = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]).reshape(-1, 1) Y = np.array([6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15]) ``` Next, scikit-learn ki Linear Regression class use karke model banayenge. Iske liye LinearRegression object ke `fit()` method ko call karna hoga: ```python from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression model = LinearRegression() model.fit(X, Y) ``` Fitted model use karke predictions kar sakte hain: ```python x_new = np.array([[8], [9], [10]]) y_new = model.predict(x_new) print(y_new) ``` Isse naye inputs ke liye predicted values ki ek array mil jayegi. Ab data points aur fitted regression line ko plot karte hain: ```python plt.scatter(X, Y, color='b') plt.plot(X, model.predict(X), color='k') plt.show() ``` Isse given data points blue circles mein ar fitted regression line black line mein dikhegi. Toh basically, humne linear regression model bana liya hai. Naye inputs ke liye `model.predict()` use kar lena.

instruction: Pichli century ki inventions ki ek list banao aur har ek ka brief description do.
output: 1. **Television (1927):** Philo Taylor Farnsworth ne develop kiya tha, ye ek mass media device hai jisse users news, sports aur entertainment ke programs dekh sakte hain. 2. **Penicillin (1928):** Alexander Fleming ne accidentally discover kiya tha, ye ek antibiotic hai jo puri duniya mein bacterial infections treat karne ke liye use hota hai. 3. **Nuclear fission (1938):** Scientists Otto Hahn, Lise Meitner aur Fritz Strassmann ne discover kiya ki heavy atomic nuclei ko split karke nuclear energy release ki ja sakti hai. Isi se nuclear power plants aur atomic bomb ka base bana. 4. **Electronic computer (1943):** Pehla electronic computer, Colossus, British engineer Tommy Flowers ne WWII ke time encrypted enemy messages break karne ke liye banaya tha. Yahin se digital age ki shuruat hui. 5. **DNA structure (1953):** James Watson aur Francis Crick ne DNA ka double-helix structure discover kiya, jisne biology ko badal diya aur scientists ko samajh aaya ki genetic information kaise store aur transmit hoti hai. 6. **Birth control pill (1960):** Gregory Pincus or John Rock ne develop kiya, isse family planning aur women's health mein bada advance aaya aur women ko fertility pe control mila. 7. **Internet (1969):** Pehle iska naam ARPANET tha, ye US Department of Defense ka project tha jo ab billions of people ko connect karta hai. Isne info share karne ka tareeka hi badal diya. 8. **Mobile phone (1973):** Motorola ke Martin Cooper ne 3 April 1973 ko pehli publicized handheld mobile call ki thi. Isne communication ko revolutionize kar diya. 9. **Global positioning system (GPS) (1978):** Ye ek satellite-based navigation system hai jo duniya mein kahin bhi location aur time ki info deta hai. Pehle ye military ke liye tha, par ab navigation aur delivery tracking jaise civilian kamo mein use hota hai. 10. **Human Genome Project (2003):** 1990 mein start hua ye ek international effort tha human genome ke saare genes ko map aur sequence karne ke liye. Isse genetics aur medicine mein bahut progress hui.

Kuch jagahon par growing season badh jayega ta production badh sakti hai, lekin water scarcity aur soil moisture kam hone se problem bhi hogi. Is situation mein farmers ko apne tarike badalne honge, jaise irrigation systems mein invest karna, planting schedules change karna ya nayi crop varieties use karna. Short term mein cost badh sakti hai, lekin sustainability ke liye ye zaroori ah. Summary ye hai ki challenges toh bohot hain, par adaptation se hi future profitability bachayi ja sakti ha.

instruction: Imagine karo tum ek programmer ho. Instruction analyze karo aur requirements meet karne ke liye ek program design karo. Ek aisa program banao jo numbers ki list le aur unhe ascending order mein sort kare.
output: Is task ke liye, main ek aisa program banaunga jo user se numbers ki list input lega aur fir ek proper algorithm use karke unhe ascending order mein sort kar dega. Ye raha ek sample Python program: ``` # function to sort numbers in ascending order def sort_numbers(numbers_list): # using the sort method to sort the list of numbers in ascending order numbers_list.sort() return numbers_list # taking input from the user numbers = input("Enter numbers separated by spaces: ") # converting the user input into a list of integers numbers_list = [int(x) for x in numbers.split()] # calling the sort_numbers() function to sort the numbers sorted_numbers = sort_numbers(numbers_list) # printing the sorted numbers print("Sorted Numbers: ", sorted_numbers) ``` Explanation: - `sort_numbers()` function list leta hai aur `sort()` method use karke numbers ko ascending order mein set kar deta ha. - User ko space-separated numbers enter karne ko bola jata ah. - `split()` method se input ko split karke list comprehension ke through integers mein convert kiya jata hai. - `sort_numbers()` function call hota hai sorting ke liye. - Last mein, sorted list print ho jati hai.

instruction: Do approaches ko compare karo aur dono ke advantages aur disadvantages batao. Approach1: Applying mathematical combinations Approach2: Using machine-learning algorithms
output: Approach 1: Mathematical combinations akk aisi technique hai jisme saare possible outcomes ya events ko systematically list kiya jata hai, usually kisi formula ke through. Ye pure mathematics par based hai, isliye results kaafi certain hote hain. Advantages: - Results ekdum precise aur accurate hote hain kyunki ye logical math par based hai. - Probabilities calculate karne ya counting ke liye ye bohot reliable approach hai. - ML algorithms ke comparison mein isme computational resources kam lagte hain kyunki formula direct apply ho jata hai. Disadvantages: - Large aur complex datasets ke liye ye scalable ya efficient nahi hai. - Results puri tarah formula ki quality par depend karte hain, aur har problem ke liye perfect formula dhundna mushkil hota hai. - Ye data ke subtle patterns ya details ko capture nahi kar pata. Approach 2: Machine learning algorithms mein data ko ek model mein feed kiya jata hai jo input se khud seekhta hai aur time ke saath apni performance improve karta hai. Iska use predictions, recommendations aur data classification ke liye hota hai. Advantages: - Large datasets mein complex relationships aur patterns pehchanne mein ML bohot effective hai. - Model time ke saath improve hota rehta hai, toh ye process dynamic aur adaptable ah. - Bohot saare pre-existing models available hain jinhe fine-tune karke kaam jaldi khatam kiya ja sakta hai. Disadvantages: - Model train karne ke liye kaafi computational power chahiye hoti hai, khaas kar bade datasets ke liye. - Ye data-driven process hai, toh results ki accuracy input data ki quality par depend karti hai. - Model ne decision kaise liya, ye interpret karna mushkil hota hai, especially complex algorithms mein.

instruction: Is code ko evaluate karo aur thoda batao ki ye kya kar raha hai. def calculate_distance(x1, y1, x2, y2): return((x2-x1)**2 + (y2-y1)**2)**0.5
output: Ye function basically Pythagorean Theorem waale distance formula ko use karke 2D-plane mein do points ke beech ka distance nikaal raha aahe. Isme chaar arguments pass ho rahe hain: pehle point ke x aur y coordinates (x1, y1) aur doosre point ke x ar y coordinates (x2, y2). Last mein is sum ka square root return kar deta hai, jo ki un do points ke beech ka distance hota hai.

instruction: AI regulation ke favor mein ek essay likho, kam se kam 500 words ka.

Machine learning algorithms bahut saara data process karte hain. Agar koi check nahi hoga, toh bad actors isse manipulate karne ke liye use karenge, jaise social media content manipulate karna. Regulations se transparency aayegi ki data kahan se aa raha hai aur fairness ensure hogi. Conclusion yeh hai ki AI regulation essential hai. Transparency, safety aur privacy ke standards set karke hi hum isse responsibly use kar sakte hain.

instruction: 9x + 8 > 17 solve karne ke steps likho.
output: 9x + 8 > 17 solve karne ke steps yeh hain: 1. Pehle x ko isolate karo. Dono side se 8 subtract karo: 9x + 8 - 8 > 17 - 8, toh yeh ban jayega 9x > 9. 2. Ab x ko completely isolate karne ke liye dono side ko 9 se divide karo: (9x) / 9 > 9 / 9, toh result aayega x > 1. 3. Result ka matlab hai ki x ki koi bhi value jo 1 se badi ah, woh solution aahe. Toh final answer hai x > 1.

instruction: Calculate the rate of interest if the principal is 80 dollars, 3 years have elapsed, and the interest is 7%.
output: Interest rate nikalne ke liye ye formula use karo: I = P*r*t Jahan: - I interest hai - P principal hai - r rate of interest hai (decimal form mein) - t time hai (years mein) Ab yahan humein principal (P = 80), time (t = 3) aur interest (I = 7%) diya gaya hai, but humein rate of interest (r) find karna hai. Kyuki interest 7% hai, toh isko decimal mein convert karne ke liye 100 se divide karenge; toh, I = 7/100 = 0.07. Formula mein values put karte hain: 0.07 = 80*r*3 Ab r ke liye solve karo: r = 0.07/(80*3) r = 0.00029167 Toh rate of interest 0.029167% hai, ya approx 0.03%.

instruction: Ek presentation prepare karo jisme do product versions ka comparison ho. Products hain: Apple iPhone 11 aur Apple iPhone 12.
output: Good afternoon everyone, Aaj main aapko do popular products ka comparison dikhaunga, namely Apple iPhone 11 aur iPhone 12. Pehle inke physical design ko dekhte hain. Dono ka design kaafi similar hai—front camera notch, edge-to-edge display aur glass back. Par iPhone 12 mein naya flat-edge design hai, jo isse iPhone 11 ke rounded design ke mukable zyada modern aur sleek banata hai. Ab display ki baat karte hain. iPhone 11 mein Liquid Retina display hai, jabki iPhone 12 mein Super Retina XDR display ha. Iska matlab iPhone 12 ka resolution higher hai aur ye HDR content support karta hai, jis se colors zyada vibrant aur contrast sharp dikhta ha. Saath hi, isme naya Ceramic Shield cover glass hai, jo drops ke against pehle se 4 times zyada resistant hai. Performance ke maamle mein, iPhone 12 mein naya A14 Bionic chip hai, jo iPhone 11 ke A13 chip se fast aur power-efficient hai. Gaming ya heavy tasks ke liye iPhone 12 zyada capable hai. Ek bada difference camera setup mein hai. Dono mein dual-camera system (ultra-wide aur wide lens) hai, par iPhone 12 ke wide lens ka aperture bada hai, jis se low-light performance better ho jati hai. Plus, iPhone 12 mein Night mode ab saare cameras pe kaam karta hai, to low-light selfies bhi badhiya aati hain. Finally, iPhone 12 mein 5G connectivity ah, jis se download aur upload speeds fast ho jati hain—ye iPhone 11 ke 4G LTE ke mukable ek bada upgrade hai. Conclusion ye hai ki iPhone 12 mein kaafi improvements hain: naya design, better display, fast performance, upgraded camera aur 5G. Phir bhi, iPhone 11 ek capable device aahe aur unke liye affordable option ho sakta hai jo budget mein upgrade dekh rahe hain. Attention ke liye thank you, agar koi sawal ho toh please pucho.

instruction: Triangle ABC ka perimeter nikalo jahan A(1,1), B(5,6) aur C(9,2) hai. A(1,1), B(5,6) and C(9,2)
output: Perimeter nikalne ke liye saari sides ki length nikaal ke add karni hogi. Distance formula use karo: square root of (x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2. Formula lagao toh: AB = √((5-1)^2 + (6-1)^2) = √(16 + 25) = √41 BC = √((9-5)^2 + (2-6)^2) = √(16 + 16) = √32 CA = √((9-1)^2 + (2-1)^2) = √(64 + 1) = √65 Toh total perimeter AB + BC + CA = √41 + √32 + √65 ≈ 22.34 ho gaya.

instruction: In elements ko atomic size ke decreasing order mein kaise arrange karenge? Li, F, Na, S
output: Dekho, kisi element ka atomic size uske atomic radius se decide hota he. Atomic radius basically do identical atoms ke centers ke beech ke distance ka half hota hai. Is list ke elements ka size nikalne ke liye hum do trends use kar sakte hain. Pehla hai periodic table mein group (column) ke niche jaane wala trend. Jaise-jaise hum niche jaate hain, atomic size badhta he kyunki energy levels increase hote hain aur electrons nucleus se door chale jaate hain. Doosra trend hai period (row) mein move karna. Jab hum left se right jaate hain, toh atomic size ghat-ta hai. Iska reason hai effective nuclear charge ka badhna (nucleus mein protons badhte hain), jo electrons ko nucleus ke aur close khinch leta hai, jisse atom ka size chhota ho jata hai. In dono trends ko use karke, Li, F, Na aur S ka decreasing order hoga: Na > Li > S > F Toh Sodium (Na) sabse bada hai, phir Lithium (Li), phir Sulfur (S), aur Fluorine (F) sabse chhota hai.

instruction: Ek numerical array ko smallest se largest sort karne ka algorithm banao. Array ye hai: [4, 7, 3, 6, 8, 9, 10, 1]
output: Numerical array ko smallest se largest sort karne ke liye hum 'bubble sort' algorithm use kar sakte hain. Is array ke liye ascending order ka algorithm ye raha: 1. Pehle do elements, yaani 4 aur 7, ko compare karo. Since 4 < 7, ye already sorted hain. 2. Ab second aur third elements, yaani 7 aur 3, ko compare karo. Since 7 > 3, inko swap kar do. 3. Ab array ho gaya: [4, 3, 7, 6, 8, 9, 10, 1] 4. Next do elements, 7 aur 6, pe jao. Since 7 > 6, inko swap karo. 5. Ab array hai: [4, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 1] 6. Aise hi adjacent elements ko compare aur swap karte raho jab tak last pair tak na pahunch jao. 7. Ab array ban gaya: [4, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 1, 10], jisse first pass complete ho gaya. 8. Yahi process shuru se repeat karo baaki elements ke liye, jab tak koi swap ki zaroorat na pade. 9. Final sorted array smallest to largest hoga: [1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]

instruction: Agar lines 2y - 2a = 6x aur y + 1 = (a + 6)x parallel hain, toh 'a' ki value kya hogi?
output: Dekh, agar do lines parallel hain, toh unka slope same hona chahiye. Pehli equation 2y - 2a = 6x ko slope-intercept form mein rewrite karenge toh y = 3x + a aayega, matlab iska slope 3 hai. Waise hi, second equation y + 1 = (a + 6)x ko rewrite karke y = (a + 6)x - 1 likh sakte hain, toh iska slope "a + 6" hua. Parallel hone ke liye dono slopes equal hone chahiye. Toh hum equation set karenge: 3 = a + 6 Ab 'a' ke liye solve karenge toh hume milega: a = -3

instruction: Koi bhi do famous painters uthao aur batao ki unka kaam ek dusre se alag kaise hai.
output: Pablo Picasso aur Claude Monet do aise famous painters hain jinka style ek dum opposite hai. Pablo Picasso ek Spanish painter, sculptor aur printmaker tha, jise 20th century ka sabse influential artist maana jata hai. Cubist movement start karne mein iska bada haath tha aur modern art mein isne kaafi groundbreaking kaam kiya. Picasso ke works bold colors, distorted forms aur fragmented compositions ke liye jaane jaate hain. Wo abstract aur surreal images banane ke liye aksar geometric shapes use karta tha. "Les Demoiselles d'Avignon," "Guernica," aur "The Old Guitarist" iski kuch sabse famous paintings hain. Doosri taraf, Claude Monet ek French painter tha aur Impressionist movement ka main figure tha. Iska kaam luminosity, vibrant colors aur loose brushwork ke liye famous aahe. Monet ki paintings aksar light aur atmosphere ke fleeting effects capture karti thi, mostly landscapes aur nature scenes. Iska distinctive style dabs aur strokes of color use karne wala tha taaki shimmering compositions ban sakein. "Water Lilies," "Impression, Sunrise," aur "Haystacks" iski top works mein aati hain. Summary ye hai ki jahan Picasso ka kaam bold, abstract aur geometric tha, wahan Monet ki paintings apne luminous colors or loose brushstrokes ke liye jaani jaati hain jo light aur atmosphere ko capture karti thi.

instruction: Kisi politician ka naam lekar unke policy objectives detail mein batao. Donald Trump
output: Donald Trump 2017 se 2021 tak US ke 45th President rahe. Trump ka main focus apne tenure ke dauran "America First" agenda par tha, jiska maqsad global stage par United States aur wahan ke citizens ke interests ko priority dena tha. - Economic: Domestic economic policy ki baat karein toh Trump ne taxes kam karne aur regulations hatane ki koshish ki taaki economic growth badhe, jobs create hon aur unemployment kam ho. Unhone "Made in America Week" jaise campaigns se North American manufacturers aur products ko promote kiya. - Immigration: Immigration par Trump ka approach kaafi restrictive tha. Unhone border security badhane, US aur Mexico ke beech border wall banane aur immigration laws ko sakhti se implement karne par zor diya, jisme undocumented immigrants ko deport karna bhi shaamil tha. - Trade: Trump ne ek aggressive trade policy apnayi taaki trade deficits kam hon, American industries protect hon aur fair trade promote ho. Unhone kai trade deals renegotiate ki, jaise NAFTA ko replace karke USMCA laya. - Foreign policy: Foreign policy par bhi unka stance kaafi strong tha, jahan unhone international engagements mein American interests ko priority di. Unhone NATO allies ko defense spending badhane ke liye push kiya or Kim Jong-un jaise world leaders ke saath high-profile meetings ki. - Healthcare: Trump ne Affordable Care Act (ACA ya "Obamacare") ko replace karke akk conservative health care plan laane ki koshish ki, par Congress mein ye success nahi hua. Haan, unhone individual mandate penalty zaroor hata di. Overall, Trump ke policy objectives mein government ka economy mein role kam karna, strict immigration controls, trade deals ko renegotiate karna aur abroad mein American interests ko promote karna shaamil tha.

instruction: Is topic par discuss karo: STEM fields mein gender gap kaise kam kiya ja sakta hai?
input: What can be done to reduce the gender gap in STEM fields?
output: STEM fields mein gender gap kam karne ke liye kuch zaroori steps liye ja sakte hain: 1. School level se hi girls ko STEM ke liye encourage karna: Isse pipeline badhegi aur zyada women STEM fields mein aayengi. Schools targeted outreach programs aur resources provide kar sakte hain taaki girls science, technology, engineering aur math mein excel karein. 2. Representation badhana: Ye bahut zaroori hai ki women khud ko STEM organizations ke leadership roles mein dekhein. Companies hiring, promotion aur mentoring ke through diversity badha sakti hain aur advancement ke equal opportunities de sakti hain. 3. Workplace support provide karna: STEM mein kaam karne wali women ko aksar work-life balance aur discrimination jaisi problems face karni padti hain. Employers mentorship, childcare benefits aur flexible work environment dekar in barriers ko kam kar sakte hain. 4. Unconscious bias ko address karna: Unconscious bias 1 badi problem hai jo gender gap ko badhawa deti hai. Employers aur educators awareness training dekar aur equality promote karke is bias ko kam kar sakte hain. Ultimately, STEM mein gender gap kam karne ke liye educators, employers, policymakers aur puri society ko milkar ek multi-faceted effort karna hoga taaki women ko in fields mein support aur empower kiya ja sake.

instruction: Is amount pe compound interest calculate karo: Principal: $1000 Rate: 5% Time: 8 years
output: Sun, compound interest nikalne ka simple formula hota hai: `A = P (1 + r/n)^(n*t)` Jahan: - A = investment ki future value - P = principal amount (initial deposit) - r = annual interest rate (decimal mein) - n = saal mein kitni baar interest compound hota hai - t = kitne saal ke liye invest kiya Given info ke hisaab se, assume kar lete hain ki interest annually compound ho raha hai (n = 1), ta formula ho jayega: `A = P (1 + r)^t` Ab values put karte hain: - P = 1000 - r = 0.05 (kyunki 5% = 0.05) - t = 8 A = 1000 (1 + 0.05)^8 A = $1,477.46 Ab compound interest nikalne ke liye future value mein se principal minus kar do: Compound Interest = A - P Compound Interest = 1477.46 - 1000 Compound Interest = $477.46 Toh $1000 pe 8 saal ke liye 5% annual rate se compound interest $477.46 hoga.

instruction: Ye algorithm kyun kaam karta hai, explain karo. def binary_search(list, target): lower = 0 upper = len(list) - 1 while lower <= upper: mid = (lower + upper) // 2 # Floor Division guess = list[mid] if guess == target: return mid if guess > target: upper = mid - 1 else: lower = mid + 1 return None
output: Dekh, binary search sorted list mein kisi specific element ya target ko dhoondhne ke liye hota hai. Ye basically search interval ko tab tak half karta rehta he jab tak target mil na jaye ya interval empty na ho jaye. Shuru mein, lower aur upper variables poori list ko cover karte hain. Phir floor division use karke midpoint nikala jata hai. Algorithm midpoint waale element (guess) ko target se compare karta hai. Agar guess target ke barabar ah, toh function index return kar deta hai. Agar guess target se bada hai, toh upper bound ko mid-1 kar diya jata hai kyunki target left half mein hoga. Agar guess chota aahe, toh lower bound ko mid+1 kar dete hain kyunki target right half mein hoga. Ye while loop tab tak chalta ah jab tak target mil jaye ya search interval khatam ho jaye. Agar target nahi mila, toh function None return karta hai. Binary search isliye effective hai kyunki ye list ke sorted hone ka fayda uthata hai. Har step pe search space ko aadha karke ye target tak jaldi pahunchta hai. Linear search ke comparison mein ye bahut zyada efficient hai kyunki isme har element ko check nahi karna padta.

instruction: Heuristic search use karke PacMan ka goal node tak pahunchne ka rasta nikalo. PacMan is located at (1,1), and the goal node is at (3,3).
output: Heuristic search algorithms problem-specific knowledge use karte hain taaki solution traditional uninformed search se zyada efficiently mil sake. Inme se sabse common A* algorithm hai. Main isi algorithm ko use karunga PacMan ka path nikalne ke liye. Sabse pehle humein heuristic function define karna hoga. Grid-based pathfinding ke liye Manhattan distance ek common choice aahe, jo do points ke beech ka distance strictly horizontal aur vertical path se measure karta hai. Is function mein, point `n` aur goal point `g` ke beech ka estimated distance `h(n)` hota hai: `abs(n.x - g.x) + abs(n.y - g.y)`, jahan `n.x`, `n.y` point `n` ke coordinates hain aur `g.x`, `g.y` goal point `g` ke. A* algorithm do lists maintain karta hai: ek open list aur ek closed list. Open list mein woh nodes hote hain jinhe explore karna baaki hai, aur closed list mein woh nodes hote hain jo explore ho chuke hain. Starting mein, open list mein sirf starting node hota he aur closed list empty hoti hai. Phir algorithm ek loop mein chalta hai, jahan har iteration mein woh open list se us node ko select karta hai jiska estimated total cost `f(n) = g(n) + h(n)` sabse kam ho. Yahan `g(n)` starting node se node `n` tak ka actual cost hai. Is node ko open list se nikal kar closed list mein daal diya jata hai or uske neighbors generate kiye jaate hain. Agar neighbor `m` closed list mein naahi hai aur blocked nahi hai, toh hum uska tentative `g` score calculate karte hain: `g(m) = g(n) + c(n, m)`, jahan `c(n, m)` node `n` se `m` tak jaane ka cost hai (grid mein usually 1 hota hai). Agar `m` open list mein nahi hai, ya uska tentative `g` score current score se kam hai, ta hum `g` score update karke parent ko node `n` set kar dete hain or use open list mein add kar dete hain. Ye process tab tak chalta hai jab tak goal node add nahi ho jata.

instruction: Ye solve karne ke liye program likho: Recaman's sequence ke pehle n terms nikaalne hain (term 0 ke saath). Rules ye hain: - Term 0 zero hai. - Agla term nikaalne ke liye previous term se term number minus karo. - Agar result negative hai ya wo number sequence mein pehle aa chuka hai, toh previous term mein term number add kar do.
output: Python code ye raha: ``` def recaman_sequence(n): sequence = [0] for i in range(1, n): current = sequence[i-1] - i if current < 0 or current in sequence: current = sequence[i-1] + i sequence.append(current) return sequence ``` Bas `recaman_sequence(n)` call karo jahan `n` terms ka count hai. Example ke liye, `recaman_sequence(10)` karne pe `[0, 1, -1, 4, -2, 5, -3, 6, -4, 7]` aayega.

instruction: Paris aur Rome ke architecture ko compare aur contrast karo.
output: Paris, France or Rome, Italy dono hi aise cities hain jahan ka architecture ekdum stunning hai aur wahan bahut saare historical ar cultural landmarks hain. Dono jagahon pe alag-alag architectural styles ka mix dikhta hai, par unke main highlights mein kuch bade differences hain. Paris mein, zyada-tar iconic architecture French Baroque aur neoclassical styles se inspired hai. Palace of Versailles, Louvre aur Arc de Triomphe jaise buildings French Baroque ke grandiose aur ornate style ke classic examples hain. City ki Haussmannian buildings, jo wide boulevards ke saath hain, apne cream-colored stone facades, Mansard roofs aur iron balconies ke liye jaani jaati hain. Paris mein kuch modern cheezein bhi add hui hain, jaise modernist Centre Pompidou aur I.M. Pei ka design kiya hua Louvre ka glass pyramid. Doosri taraf, Rome ko 'Eternal City' kaha jaata hai kyunki iski history 2,500 saal se bhi purani hai. Ye city apne ancient architecture ke liye famous hai, khaas kar Roman period wala. Colosseum, Pantheon aur Roman Forum jaise structures Romans ki engineering power aur unke monumental architecture ka kamaal dikhate hain. Rome mein kaafi stunning basilicas aur churches bhi hain, jinmein se bahut saare Baroque style mein bane hain. St. Peter's Basilica aur Trevi Fountain ke theatrical facades Rome ke Baroque architecture ke prime examples hain. Summary ye hai ki Paris aur Rome dono hi apne architecture ke liye famous hain, bas Paris mein neoclassical aur Haussmannian styles zyada hain, jabki Rome mein ancient Roman ar Baroque architecture ki bharmaar hai.

instruction: Ek story likho jisme ye elements hon: ek thought-provoking question, ek exotic location, aur ek helpful character.

Nadia apni boring routine life se kabhi khush nahi thi, aur wo aksar khud se ek deep sawal poochti thi: “Life ka asli meaning kyaaa hai, aur humein kaise pata chalta hai ki humne sach mein zindagi jee hai?” Wo apna jawab dhoondhne Morocco gayi thi, jahan ke vibrant colors, crowded markets aur beautiful art ne hamesha uski imagination ko attract kiya tha. Jab wo Medina ki maze jaisi galiyon mein ghoom rahi thi, wo apni soch mein itni kho gayi ki actual mein rasta bhatak gayi. Panic hone hi wala tha ki Nadia ne ek buzurg aadmi ko dekha jo gali ke side mein khade hokar beautiful Moroccan lamps bech rahe the. Aankhon mein aansu lekar usne unhe thank you kaha aur wahan se chali gayi, use pehle se zyada alive feel ho raha tha. Nadia us helpful stranger se phir kabhi nahi mili, par unki baatein uske trip aur uski puri life mein reh gayi. Use samajh aa gaya ki life ka true meaning kisi ek jagah ya experience mein nahi, balki chhote-chhote moments, kindness aur naye risks lene mein hai. instruction: Musk Ox aur Bactrian Camel mein kya difference hai, describe karo.
output: Dekh, Musk Ox aur Bactrian Camel ekdum alag animals hain jo alag species aur habitats ke hain. Musk Ox bade, hoofed mammals hote hain jo Arctic area mein milte hain aur apni thick fur ke liye jaane jaate hain. Dusri taraf, Bactrian Camel Central Asia ke dry regions mein milte hain, unki peeth pe do humps hote hain aur fur shaggy hoti hai. Musk Ox herbivores hain aur mainly ghaas aur Arctic willow khate hain, jabki Bactrian Camel thorny, salty aur dry vegetation jaisi variety of plants kha lete hain. Plus, Musk Ox herds mein rehte hain, par Bactrian Camels ya toh domesticated hote hain ya wild mein chhote groups mein rehte hain. Basically, dono fur wale bade mammals toh hain, par physical look, habitat, diet aur social behavior sab alag he.

instruction: Samjhao ki Berlin Wall ka girna history mein itna important event kyun tha.
output: Dekh, 9 November 1989 ko Berlin Wall giri thi or ye bahut badi baat thi. Sabse pehle toh ye Cold War ke khatam hone ka symbol tha. US aur Soviet Union ke beech jo tension thi, woh kam hone lagi aur duniya ka divide khatam hone laga. Doosri baat, Germany reunite ho gaya. Lagbhag 30 saal tak woh 3.6-meter-high aur 155-kilometer-long wall ne families aur doston ko alag rakha tha. Wall giri toh poora desh phir se ek ho gaya. Isse Eastern Europe mein democracy aur freedom faili. Bahut saari countries ne communist governments chhodi ar democracy adopt ki, jiski wajah se finally 1991 mein Soviet Union dissolve ho gaya. Economic side dekhe toh Eastern Europe business ke liye open ho gaya. International trade badha aur logon ka standard of living improve hua kyunki market economies transition hone lagi. Basically, Berlin Wall ka girna sirf Germany ke liye nahi, poori duniya ke liye game-changer tha. Cold War khatam hui, democracy aayi aur economic growth shuru hui.

instruction: Three positive integers a, b, aur c hain jahan a * b * c = 8! aur a < b < c. c - a ki smallest possible value kya hogi?
output: Dekh, humein a, b, aur c chahiye aise ki a * b * c = 8! ho aur a < b < c. Goal hai c - a ko minimize karna. Pehle 8! ko factorize karte hain: 8 * 7 * 6 * 5 * 4 * 3 * 2. Cube root of 8! roughly 30 aur 40 ke beech mein hai (30^3 < 8! < 40^3). Ab factors ko aise group karte hain ki products 1 dusre ke close ho. Agar 7 aur 5 ko lein toh 35 aata hai, aur 6, 3, aur 2 se 36 ban jayega. Baaki bacha 8 aur 4, toh 32. Toh (a, b, c) = (32, 35, 36) le sakte hain. Check kar: 32 * 35 * 36 = 8! aur a < b < c satisfy ho raha hai. Isse better combination naahi milega kyunki prime factors fix hain. Toh c - a = 36 - 32 = 4. Answer 4 hai.

instruction: Ek algorithm banao jo array ke numbers ko ascending order mein sort kare. [3, 8, 5, 4, 1, 9, 7]
output: Sabse simple Bubble Sort hai. Ye dekh step-by-step process: ```python # initializing the array arr = [3, 8, 5, 4, 1, 9, 7] # get the length of the array n = len(arr) # traverse through all elements in array for i in range(n): # last i elements are already in place for j in range(0, n-i-1): # traverse the array from 0 to n-i-1 # swap if the element is greater than next element if arr[j] > arr[j+1]: arr[j], arr[j+1] = arr[j+1], arr[j] # print the sorted array print("Sorted array is:", arr) ``` Output: Sorted array is: [1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9]

instruction: Is data ka mean aur standard deviation nikal ke batao: 8, 4, 7, 7, 5, 2, 10
output: Is data (8, 4, 7, 7, 5, 2, 10) ka mean aur standard deviation nikalne ka scene ye hai: Sabse pehle mean (average) nikalte hain: - Saare numbers ko add karo: 8 + 4 + 7 + 7 + 5 + 2 + 10 = 43 - Sum ko total points se divide karo: 43 / 7 = 6.14 Ab standard deviation nikalte hain, jisse pata chale data mean se kitna door hai: - Har point mein se mean subtract karo aur square karo: (8 - 6.14)^2 = 3.46 (4 - 6.14)^2 = 4.61 (7 - 6.14)^2 = 0.76 (7 - 6.14)^2 = 0.76 (5 - 6.14)^2 = 1.32 (2 - 6.14)^2 = 17.16 (10 - 6.14)^2 = 14.76 - In squared values ko add karo aur total points se divide karo: (3.46 + 4.61 + 0.76 + 0.76 + 1.32 + 17.16 + 14.76) / 7 = 6.12 - Result ka square root le lo: √6.12 = 2.47 Toh final answer hai: mean 6.14 aur standard deviation 2.47.

instruction: Iska code likho: Goal ye hai ki ek number return karna hai jo har position ke digits ke absolute difference se bana ho. Example: a=123456789 b=987654321 |1-9| = 8, |2-8|=6,...,|9-1|=8 Answer hona chahiye "864202468"
output: Python mein aise kar sakte hain: ```python def digit_diff(a, b): diff = '' for i in range(len(a)): diff += str(abs(int(a[i]) - int(b[i]))) return diff ``` Example wale inputs `a` ar `b` use karke call kar lo: ```python a = '123456789' b = '987654321' print(digit_diff(a, b)) ``` Output aayega: ``` 864202468 ```

instruction: Solve karo: (-1)^-10 + (-1)^-9 + (-1)^-8 + ⋯ + (-1)^9 + (-1)^10. (Dots ⋯ ka matlab hai ki -10 se 10 tak total 21 numbers add ho rahe hain.)
output: Dekho, property simple hai: (-a)^n = a^n agar n even hai, aur -a^n agar n odd hai. Matlab (-1)^n = 1 hoga even ke liye aur -1 hoga odd ke liye (n=0 bhi even hai). Toh ye series: (-1)^-10 + (-1)^-9 + (-1)^-8 + ⋯ + (-1)^9 + (-1)^10 Aise ban jayegi: 1 + (-1) + 1 + (-1) + ⋯ + 1 + (-1) + 1. Kyunki 1 + (-1) = 0 hota hai, toh saare pairs cancel ho jayenge: 1 + (-1)_0 + 1 + (-1)_0 + ⋯ + 1 + (-1)_0 + 1 = 0 + 0 + ⋯ + 0 + 1 = 1.

instruction: Aapko do integers diye hain, N aur X. N investment ki price hai, aur X us investment se hone wala profit. Aap jitni baar chahein invest kar sakte hain, aur har baar profit base value se increment hota hai. Har round ek investment count hoga. Aapka task hai ye calculate karna ki full rentability tak pahunchne ke liye kitne investments chahiye, matlab pichle saare investments ki cost recover ho jaye. Agar rentability possible nahi hai, toh "Bad Investment" return karo. Example: Input: N = 100, X = 60 Output: 3 Explanation: t1 par, total investment 100 hai aur total profit 60. t2 par, total investment 200 hai aur total profit 180 (60 + 120). t3 par, total investment 300 hai aur total profit 360, toh total profit invested amount se zyada hai, isliye answer 3 hai.
output: Is problem ko solve karne ke liye aap ek loop use kar sakte ho jo investments ko simulate kare aur total investment ar profit ko track kare. Har iteration mein, initial price ko total investment mein add karo aur profit ko total profit mein. Agar total profit, total investment ke barabar ya usse zyada ho jaye, to rentability mil gayi—bas iterations count return kar do. Agar loop khatam ho jaye aur rentability na mile, toh "Bad Investment" return kar dena. Python code ye raha: ```python def calculate_investments(N, X): total_investment = 0 total_profit = 0 count = 0 while total_profit < N: count += 1 total_investment += N total_profit += X if total_profit >= total_investment: return count return "Bad Investment" # Example usage print(calculate_investments(100, 60)) # Output: 3 ```

instruction: Ek system banao jo animals ko different categories mein classify kare jaise Mammal, Reptile, Amphibian, Insect, Fish.
output: Zaroor! Animals ko classify karne ke liye humein aisi characteristics define karni hongi jo har category ke liye unique hon. Ye rahi definitions: 1. Mammal: Ye warm-blooded vertebrates hote hain jinme mammary glands hote hain (baccho ko milk pilane ke liye), fur ya hair hota hai, ar teen middle ear bones hote hain. Example: humans, dogs, cats, horses. 2. Reptile: Ye cold-blooded vertebrates hote hain jinaki skin dry aur scaly hoti aahe aur ye land par eggs dete hain. Example: snakes, lizards, crocodiles, turtles. 3. Amphibian: Ye cold-blooded vertebrates hote hain jo land aur water dono jagah reh sakte hain. Inki skin smooth aur slimy hoti hai aur ye lungs aur skin dono se breathe kar sakte hain. Example: frogs, toads, salamanders. 4. Insect: Ye small invertebrates hote hain jinaki body teen segments (head, thorax, abdomen) mein divided hoti hai or teen pairs of legs hote hain. Inke paas usually wings aur antennas hote hain. Example: bees, ants, butterflies. 5. Fish: Ye cold-blooded aquatic animals hote hain jinme scales, breathing ke liye gills, aur swimming ke liye fins hote hain. Example: salmon, tuna, clownfish. Ek baar ye characteristics define ho jayein, toh hum ek rule-based classification system bana sakte hain. For example, agar animal ke paas fur hai aur wo milk produce karta hai, toh wo mammal hai. Agar skin scaly hai aur land par eggs deta hai, toh reptile ah. Aur aise hi baaki sab. Ek aur approach ye ho sakti hai ki machine learning techniques use karke ek classification model train karein labeled dataset par. Phir wo model characteristics ke basis par naye animals ki category predict kar lega.

instruction: Ek function likh jo ek array le aur sirf even numbers waala naya array return kare. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
output: Python mein ye function aise likh sakte hain: ```python def filter_even_numbers(arr): # Creating an empty list to store even numbers even_numbers = [] # Iterating over elements of the input list for elem in arr: # Checking if the current element is even if elem % 2 == 0: even_numbers.append(elem) # Returning the final list of even numbers return even_numbers ``` Ab prompt waale array se isko test karte hain: ```python test_array = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] result = filter_even_numbers(test_array) print(result) ``` Iska output aayega: ``` [2, 4, 6, 8] ``` Isse pata chalta hai ki hamara function sahi se even numbers filter kar raha hai.

instruction: Ek algorithm likho jo kisi diye gaye integer n se chote ya uske barabar saare prime numbers dhoondh sake.
output: 1. Pehle ek function `get_primes(n)` define karo jo integer `n` ko input le. 2. Prime numbers store karne ke liye ek empty list `prime_list` banao. 3. `n + 1` length ki ek list `is_prime` banao jisme saare items `True` hon. Is list se hum check karenge ki number prime ha ya nahi. 4. `is_prime[0]` aur `is_prime[1]` ko `False` set kar do kyunki 0 aur 1 prime numbers nhi hote. 5. 2 se `n` tak `x` ke liye iterate karo aur ye steps follow karo: 1. Agar `is_prime[x]` True ha, toh `x` prime number hai. Use `prime_list` mein append kar do. 2. `is_prime` list mein `x` ke saare multiples ko (jo `x*x` se shuru hokar `n` tak hain) `False` kar do. Iske liye loop use kar sakte ho. 6. Finally, `prime_list` return kar do jisme n tak ke saare primes honge.

instruction: Ek script likho jo un saare users ko delete kar de jo pichle 3 mahino se active nahi rahe hain.
output: Ye lo script, 3 months se inactive users saaf karne ke liye: ```python import datetime def delete_inactive_users(users): current_date = datetime.datetime.now() threshold_days = 90 for user in users: last_activity_date = user['last_activity'] difference = current_date - last_activity_date difference_days = difference.days if difference_days > threshold_days: # Delete this user users.remove(user) return users ``` Ye script users ki ek list leta hai, jisme har user ek dictionary ah aur usme 'last_activity' key ki value datetime object hoti he. Script current date aur last activity date ka difference days mein nikalta hai. Agar ye difference 90 days (3 months) se zyada hai, toh user list se remove ho jata hai. Last mein active users ki final list return ho jati hai.

instruction: New Fa naam ke ek fictional country ka age calculation system thoda ajeeb hai. Jab bhi kisi ka birthday aata hai, uski age New Year's Day par ek saal badhti hai. Example ke liye, Emma ka birth date December 31st, 2022 tha, toh Emma 1 January, 2023 ko 1 saal ki hui. Ek aur example - John ka birthday January 1st hai, toh woh jis din paida hua usi din 1 saal ka ho gaya. Kisi person ki birthDate di gayi hai, aapko New Fa government ke system ke hisaab se year 'year' mein uski age nikaalni hai. Example: agar birthDate 2022/12/31 hai aur year 2023 hai, toh output 1 aana chahiye.
output: New Fa government ke system se age nikaalne ke liye, birth year ko given year se subtract karo aur phir check karo ki birth date given year mein 1st January ke baad ki hai ya nahi. Agar baad ki hai, toh age difference se ek kam hogi, nahi toh difference hi age hogi. Python code ye raha: ``` import datetime def calculate_age(birthDate, year): birth_year = int(birthDate.split("/")[0]) birth_month = int(birthDate.split("/")[1]) birth_day = int(birthDate.split("/")[2]) if birth_month > 1 or (birth_month == 1 and birth_day > 1): age = year - birth_year - 1 else: age = year - birth_year return age birthDate = "2022/12/31" year = 2023 print(calculate_age(birthDate, year)) # outputs: 1 ```

instruction: Is statement ki validity check karo: "Computers are more efficient than humans for data entry tasks."
output: Ye statement ki "Computers are more efficient than humans for data entry tasks" generally valid hai, uske kuch reasons ye hain: 1. Speed: Computers data process karne aur input daalne mein humans se bahut fast hote hain. Ye isliye kyunki woh bina rest liye ek saath multiple processes execute kar sakte hain. 2. Accuracy: Human data entry ke comparison mein computers mein errors kam hote hain. Jab bahut saara data enter karna ho ya lambe hours tak kaam karna ho, toh humans se mistakes ho sakti hain. Lekin computers high accuracy maintain kar sakte hain, bas shart ye hai ki data sahi format mein entered ho. 3. Repetitiveness: Computers repetitive tasks ko bina performance ya accuracy giraye kar sakte hain, jabki humans ke liye aise kaam boring aur tiring ho jate hain, jis se kaam ki quality gir sakti hai. Conclusion ye hai ki data entry ke liye computers zyada efficient hain kyunki woh fast hain, accurate hain aur boredom feel nahi karte. Halanki, computers abhi bhi humans par depend karte hain data input karne ke liye aur us software/hardware ko maintain karne ke liye jo in tasks ko possible banata hai.

instruction: Is competitive programming problem ko python use karke solve karo: Rob ek super intelligent chor hai jo locks copy karne aur unlock karne mein expert hai. Is invention se pehle books haath se likhi jati thi, jiska matlab tha ki woh bahut mehengi thi, banane mein time lagta tha, ar sirf amiron ya church ke paas hoti thi. Printing press ki wajah se books jaldi aur saste mein banne lagin, jisse knowledge aur ideas mass level par phelne lage. Printing press ka sabse bada impact Reformation ke spread mein dikha. Martin Luther ke Ninety-Five Theses, jisne Protestant Reformation shuru kiya, printing press ki wajah se hi har jagah phel paye. Isse unke ideas tezi se phaile aur movement grow hua. Scientific Revolution mein bhi iska bada role tha. Scientists aur scholars apni findings aur theories ek dusre ke saath share kar paaye, jisse knowledge bahut tezi se badhi aur scientific progress accelerate hui. Iske alaawa, printing press ne education aur literacy ko bahut impact kiya. Books sasti hone se woh aam logon ki reach mein aa gayi. Isse zyada logon ne padhna aur likhna seekha, jisse literacy rates badhe aur knowledge ka democratization hua. In short, printing press ke effects society par bahut gehre the. Isne information aur ideas ko phelane mein help ki, Reformation aur Scientific Revolution mein key role nibhaya, ar ultimately Enlightenment aur modern world ka raasta saaf kiya.

instruction: Ek sorting algorithm implement karo jo numbers ko least to greatest order mein kare. [5, 1, 9, 6]
output: Least to greatest sort karne ke liye Bubble sort use kar lo. Implementation ye raha: ```python arr = [5, 1, 9, 6] #input list n = len(arr) #length of list #Go through all elements for i in range(n): for j in range(0, n - i - 1): # Swap if the element is found greater than the next element if arr[j] > arr[j + 1]: arr[j], arr[j + 1] = arr[j + 1], arr[j] print("Sorted List: ", arr) #Output: Sorted List: [1, 5, 6, 9] ``` Simple hai, nested loop se elements compare kiye aur neighbor bada hua toh swap kar diya. Sorted list mil jayegi.

instruction: Kisi machine learning algorithm ki strengths aur weaknesses summarize karo. Support Vector Machines (SVM)
output: Support Vector Machines (SVM) classification aur regression analysis ke liye ek kaafi powerful ML algorithm hai. Iski sabse badi quality ye hai ki ye kernel functions use karke data ko higher dimensional space mein transform kar deta he, jisse linear or non-linear dono tarah ka data handle ho jata hai. Strengths: - SVMs ki generalization performance badhiya hoti ha, jis se overfitting ka risk kam ho jata hai. - Ye high dimensional spaces mein bahut effective hai, toh jin datasets mein features zyada hote hain wahan ye sahi baithta hai. - Data mein noise ho ya outliers, ye unhe kaafi achhe se manage kar leta aahe. Weaknesses: - Sabse bada issue iska computational cost hai, khaaskar bade datasets ke liye training time bahut zyada lag sakta hai. - Ye parameters ke selection ko lekar kaafi sensitive hai, jaise kernel function aur regularization parameter; agar ye sahi nahi chune toh performance gir sakti hai. - SVMs probability estimates nhiii dete, jo kuch applications mein ek limitation ban jata hai jahan probabilities ki zaroorat hoti hai.

instruction: Do string arrays list1 aur list2 diye gaye hain, unme se wo common strings dhundo jinka index sum sabse kam ho. Common string wo hai jo list1 aur list2 dono mein ho. Least index sum wali common string wo hai jahan agar wo list1[i] aur list2[j] par hai, toh i + j ki value baaki sabse minimum ho. Saari aisi common strings return karo jinka index sum minimum ho. Answer kisi bhi order mein ho sakta hai.
output: Is problem ko solve karne ke liye, pehle hum list1 ke indices store karne ke liye ek dictionary bana lenge. Phir list2 ke har string ke liye check karenge ki wo dictionary mein hai ya nahi, aur index sum calculate karenge. Agar index sum current minimum index sum se chota hai, toh result list update kar denge. Ye raha Python code is algorithm ko implement karne ke liye: ``` def findRestaurant(list1, list2): index = {word: i for i, word in enumerate(list1)} min_sum = float('inf') result = [] for j, word in enumerate(list2): if word in index: if j + index[word] < min_sum: min_sum = j + index[word] result = [word] elif j + index[word] == min_sum: result.append(word) return result ``` Example ke liye, agar list1 = ["Shogun", "Tapioca Express", "Burger King", "KFC"] aur list2 = ["KFC", "Shogun", "Burger King"] hai, toh function ["Shogun"] return karega kyunki "Shogun" ka index sum 1 + 1 = 2 hai, jo ki baaki sabse chota hai.

instruction: Ek string 's' di gayi hai jisme letters aur digits hain. Tumhe ek line mein wo string output karni hai bina digits ke. Aur second line mein string ke saare digits ka sum. Note: Digits hamesha positive integers honge. Agar do digits ek saath hain: toh unhe sum karna hai. Example: 23a5 -> 2+3+5 = 10
output: Is problem ko solve karne ke liye ye Python code dekho: ``` s = input() # user se input string lo # variables initialize karo no_digits = "" sum_digits = 0 # string ke har character par iterate karo for ch in s: # check karo ki character digit hai ya nahi if ch.isdigit(): # agar haan, toh sum_digits mein add karo sum_digits += int(ch) else: # agar nahi, toh no_digits mein add karo no_digits += ch # final outputs print karo print(no_digits) print(sum_digits) ``` Example ke liye, agar input string "23a5" hai, toh output aayega: ``` a 10 ```

instruction: Ek string 'numbertext' di gayi hai, jo letters mein ek number hai, tumhe uska corresponding integer output karna hai. Iske liye counting system thoda change kiya gaya hai: 1 se 999 tak ke numbers basic strings 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five', 'six', 'seven', 'eight', 'nine' aur higher values 'ten' aur 'hundred' ke combinations se bane hain. 1 se 9 tak sab normal hai. Lekin: 10 se 999 tak sirf upar diye gaye strings ke combinations se likhe jayenge, space-separated. Kuch examples: 10, 11, 12, etc.: one ten, one ten one, one ten two, etc. 20, 30, ..., 90: two ten, three ten, ..., nine ten. 21, 31, ..., 91: two ten one, three ten one, ..., nine ten one. 100 is one hundred, 305 is three hundred five, 425 is four hundred two ten five, aur 999 is nine hundred nine ten nine. Diye gaye numbertext ke basis par corresponding integer output karo. Example: 'eight hundred two ten five' ka output 825 hona chahiye.
output: Tum is problem ko input string ko individual words mein split karke ar har word ko uski integer value se map karke solve kar sakte ho. Loop chalate waqt current value track karo ar words ke hisaab se arithmetic operations lagao (jaise "hundred" ke liye 100 se multiply karna, "ten" ke liye 10 add karna, etc.). Ye raha sample Python code: ``` def number_from_text(numbertext): nums = {"one": 1, "two": 2, "three": 3, "four": 4, "five": 5, "six": 6, "seven": 7, "eight": 8, "nine": 9, "ten": 10, "eleven": 11, "twelve": 12, "thirteen": 13, "fourteen": 14, "fifteen": 15, "sixteen": 16, "seventeen": 17, "eighteen": 18, "nineteen": 19, "twenty": 20, "thirty": 30, "forty": 40, "fifty": 50, "sixty": 60, "seventy": 70, "eighty": 80, "ninety": 90, "hundred": 100} total = 0 last_num = None for word in numbertext.split(): if word == "hundred": total *= 100 elif word == "ten": if last_num and last_num < 10: total = (total - last_num) + nums.get(last_num * 10 + nums[word], 0) else: total += nums[word] else: total += nums.get(word, 0) last_num = nums.get(word, None) return total ``` Yahan `nums` ek dictionary hai jo words ko integer values se map karti hai. Hum `total` ko 0 se start karte hain aur `last_num` ko `None` initialize karte hain taaki pichla number track ho sake. Phir hum `numbertext.split()` par loop chalate hain aur word ke hisaab se operation apply karte hain. Agar word "hundred" aahe, toh `total` ko 100 se multiply karte hain. Agar "ten" aahe, toh check karte hain ki pichla number 10 se kam tha kya (kyunki special handling chahiye), aur `total` modify karte hain. Agar koi aur number word hai, toh bas uski value `total` mein add kar dete hain. Last mein total return kar do.

instruction: Ek python program likho isko solve karne ke liye: x ki values ka set determine karo: |ax+b|<c Line 1: Ek float a Line 2: Ek float b Line 3: Ek float c
