instruction: Is formula aur teen variables ko use karke ek theorem banao. Formula: A + B = C Variables: D, E, F
output: Theorem: Maan lo A + B = C hai. Agar hum dono sides mein D add karein, toh left side ka sum right side ke equal hoga. Yaani, A + B + D = C + D. Ab agar E = C + D hai, toh hum use substitute karke likh sakte hain A + B + D = E. Phir se, agar dono sides mein F add karein toh A + B + D + F = E + F ho jayega, jiska matlab hai A, B, D aur F ka sum E aur F ke sum ke equal hai. Toh final theorem ye hai ki agar A + B = C aur E = C + D hai, to A + B + D + F = E + F hoga.

instruction: 5 balls ko 3 boxes mein kitne tareekon se daal sakte hain agar balls indistinguishable hain par boxes distinguishable?
output: Dekh, balls indistinguishable hain, toh humein sirf ye dekhna hai ki kis box mein kitni balls hain. (5,0,0) ke 3 ways hain (matlab box 1 mein 5, ya box 2 mein 5, ya box 3 mein 5). (4,1,0) aur (3,2,0) ke liye 3! = 6 ways each hain; kyunki humein 3 boxes mein se ek ko max balls dena hai aur ek ko empty chhodna hai. Lekin (3,1,1) aur (2,2,1) ke sirf 3-3 ways hain; kyunki yahan bas ek box aisa hoga jisme balls ki count different ho. Toh total ho gaya: 3 + 6 + 6 + 3 + 3 = 21 arrangements.

instruction: Traditional machine learning model ke bajaye deep learning model use karne ke kya benefits hain?
output: Traditional ML models ke comparison mein deep learning ke kaafi fayde hain: 1. Automated feature engineering: Traditional ML mein success is baat par depend karti hai ki aapne features sahi choose kiye ya nahi, jisme bahut time aur expertise lagta hai. Wahi deep learning models raw data se khud hi meaningful features aur complex patterns seekh lete hain. 2. Complex data handle karna: Deep learning unstructured aur structured dono tarah ka data handle kar sakta hai, jaise images, sound, aur text. Iske hierarchical layers raw data se high-level abstract features nikaal lete hain. 3. Efficiency aur scalability: Deep learning algorithms bade datasets par train hone ke liye bane hain, isliye massive data volumes par ye zyada efficient hote hain. Time ke saath model aur accurate hota jata hai, toh preprocessing ki zaroorat kam padti hai. 4. Behtar accuracy: Complex data jaise images ya speech ke case mein deep learning models traditional ML se zyada accuracy dete hain. 5. Adaptability: Deep learning models nayi situations ke hisaab se adapt kar sakte hain aur continuous learning se improve hote rehte hain. Isliye ye dynamic environments ke liye best hain. Lekin ek baat yaad rakhna, deep learning models ko train karne ke liye zyada data ar computational resources chahiye hote hain, aur ye hamesha traditional ML se behtar nahi hote. Choice data ki complexity, resources aur desired outcome par depend karti hai.

instruction: Iska Python solution likho: Ek binary array 'nums' diya gaya hai, usme maximum consecutive 1's return karo.
input: Given a binary array nums, return the maximum number of consecutive 1's in the array.
output: Binary array mein max consecutive 1's nikaalne ka Python solution ye raha: ``` def find_max_consecutive_ones(nums): max_count = 0 curr_count = 0 for num in nums: if num == 1: curr_count += 1 max_count = max(max_count, curr_count) else: curr_count = 0 return max_count ``` Tum is function ko binary array pass karke call kar sakte ho aur ye max consecutive 1's return kar dega. Example: ``` binary_array = [1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1] max_consecutive_ones = find_max_consecutive_ones(binary_array) print(max_consecutive_ones) # Output: 3 ```

instruction: Ek web developer ko web page ka size design karna hai. Ek specific rectangular web page ka area diya gaya hai, toh tumhe ek aisa rectangular page design karna hai jisme length L aur width W ye requirements satisfy karein: 1. Design kiye gaye page ka area target area ke equal hona chahiye. 2. Width W, length L se badi nahi honi chahiye (L >= W). 3. L aur W ka difference jitna ho sake utna kam hona chahiye. Ek array [L, W] return karo jisme length aur width sequence mein hon.
output: Requirements ke hisaab se rectangular web page design karne ke liye ye steps follow karo: 1. Target area ka square root nikaalo. 2. Square root ko nearest integer tak round up karo, ye tumhara length L hoga. 3. Target area ko length L se divide karke width W nikaalo. 4. Agar width W integer nahi ha, toh usko nearest integer tak round up kar do. 5. [L, W] array return kar do. Is logic ko implement karne wala function ye raha: ``` function designWebPage(targetArea) { const L = Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(targetArea)); const W = Math.ceil(targetArea / L); return [L, W]; } ``` Tum function ko target area pass karke aise call kar sakte ho: ``` const targetArea = 24; const [L, W] = designWebPage(targetArea); console.log(`Length: ${L}, Width: ${W}`); ``` Iska output aayega: ``` Length: 5, Width: 5 ``` Iska matlab designed page ki length 5 aur width 5 hai, jiska area 25 hai, jo ki target area 24 ke bahut close hai.

instruction: Is task ke liye do methods ko compare karo. Task: Do points ke beech shortest path find karna
output: Graph pe shortest path find karne ke liye Dijkstra's algorithm aur A* algorithm kaafi popular hain. Dono ka comparison dekhte hain. Dijkstra's ek graph-search algorithm aahe jo weighted graph mein shortest path nikaal leta hai. Ye har vertex ko ek tentative distance assign karta hai—initial vertex 0 hota hai aur baaki sab infinity. Phir ye har vertex pe jaakar apne neighbours ki distance update karta hai. Jab saare vertices visit ho jaate hain, toh humein initial vertex se baaki sabka shortest distance mil jata hai. A* algorithm ki baat karein toh ye ek informed search algorithm ah jo heuristics use karta he. Ye bhi Dijkstra ki tarah distance assign karta hai, par saath mein ek heuristic value bhi deta hai jo destination tak ka estimated distance batati hai. A* in dono values ka sum use karke decide karta hai ki agla vertex kaunsa visit karna hai, taaki kam se kam vertices check karne padein. Performance wise, A* generally fast hota hai kyunki heuristics help karte hain. Par A* ki efficiency heuristic function ki accuracy pe depend karti hai; agar function sahi nahi hai, toh ye Dijkstra se behtar nahi hoga. Simple hai, dono effective hain, par best method graph ki characteristics pe depend karega.

instruction: Aisa kaunsa prime number hai jo ek perfect square se 4 zyada hai aur next perfect square se 7 kam hai?
output: Humein ek aisa prime number dhoondna ah jo do conditions satisfy kare: wo ek perfect square se 4 bada ho, or agle perfect square se 7 chota. Maan lo wo prime number 'n' hai. Agar hum n mein se 4 minus karein, toh humein ek perfect square milega—isko (n-4) = a^2 maan lete hain. Aur agar n mein 7 add karein, toh next perfect square milega—yaani (n+7) = b^2. Kyunki b, a ke baad wala next perfect square hai, toh b = a + 1 hoga. Ab equation banate hain: b^2 - a^2 = (b-a)(b+a) = (a+1-a)(a+1+a) = 2a + 1 Problem ke hisaab se b^2 - a^2 = 11 hona chahiye. Toh: 2a + 1 = 11 Isse a = 5 aata aahe. Toh wo perfect square jo n se 4 kam hai, wo 25 hai (a^2 = 25), aur agla perfect square 36 hai (6^2 = 36). Iska matlab n = 29 hoga, jo ki ek prime number hai aur dono conditions satisfy karta hai.

instruction: Ek array ko ascending order mein sort karne ka code likho. [25, 32, 10, 17, 9]
output: Python mein Bubble Sort use kar lete hain, kaafi simple hai. Isme bas adjacent elements ko baar-baar compare karke swap karte hain agar wo wrong order mein hon. ```python array = [25, 32, 10, 17, 9] def bubbleSort(arr): n = len(arr) # Traverse through all array elements for i in range(n-1): for j in range(0, n-i-1): # Swap if the element found is greater than the next element if arr[j] > arr[j+1] : arr[j], arr[j+1] = arr[j+1], arr[j] bubbleSort(array) print ("Sorted array is: ", array) ``` Output: Sorted array is: [9, 10, 17, 25, 32]

instruction: Do vectors ke beech ka angle calculate karo. Vector A = (3, 4) Vector B = (4, 3)
output: Do vectors ke beech ka angle dot product formula use karke nikala ja sakta hai: Agar vector A = (x1, y1) aur vector B = (x2, y2) hai, ta dot product A.B = x1*x2 + y1*y2 hota hai. Vector A ka magnitude |A| = sqrt(x1^2 + y1^2) hota hai. Angle ka cosine is formula se nikalta hai: cos(θ) = (A.B) / (|A||B|) Hamare case mein: Vector A = (3, 4) Vector B = (4, 3) A.B = 3*4 + 4*3 = 24 |A| = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5 |B| = sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = 5 cos(θ) = (A.B) / (|A||B|) = 24 / (5*5) = 0.96 θ = arccos(0.96) = 16.26 degrees Toh basically, vector A or vector B ke beech ka angle approximately 16.26 degrees hai.

instruction: Customer churn predict karne ke liye ek model banao. Dataset mein customer demographic data, activity data aur churn information hai.

instruction: Ek algorithm design karo is problem ko solve karne ke liye: Ek NxN matrix di gayi hai, usme se smallest positive integer dhoondo jo missing hai.
output: Dekh, smallest missing positive integer nikalne ka ek simple approach batata hoon: 1. Ek set bana le taaki matrix ke saare positive integers ko track kiya ja sake. 2. Matrix ke har element pe iterate kar: a. Agar element positive integer hai, toh usey set mein add kar de. 3. Ek variable `missing` le aur usey 1 set kar, jo smallest positive missing integer represent karega. 4. Ek loop chala jo `True` rahe: a. Check kar ki kya `missing` set mein present hai. b. Agar hai, to `missing` ki value ko 1 se increment kar de. c. Agar nahi hai, ta loop se break kar ja. 5. Finally, `missing` ki value ko result ki tarah return kar de. Is algorithm ka Python implementation aisa dikhega: ```python def findSmallestMissing(matrix): presentIntegers = set() for row in matrix: for element in row: if element > 0: presentIntegers.add(element) missing = 1 while True: if missing not in presentIntegers: break missing += 1 return missing ```

instruction: Integers ki ek list ko smallest to largest sort karne ke liye ek algorithm ka example do.
output: Sorting ke liye ek common example 'Bubble sort' algorithm hai. Ye aise kaam karta hai: 1. List ke pehle element se start kar aur current element ko next element se compare kar. 2. Agar current element next wale se bada ha, toh dono ki positions swap kar de. Agar nahi, toh unhe waise hi rehne de ar next element pe move kar. 3. Ye process tab tak repeat kar jab tak list ke end tak na pahunch jaye. 4. Jab end tak pahunch jaye, toh phir se pehle element se ye process shuru kar. 5. Ye steps tab tak repeat kar jab tak puri list ascending order mein sort na ho jaye (yaani jab tak koi swap ki zaroorat na pade). 6. Finally, sorted list return kar de. Example ke liye, maan lo hamare paas ye list hai: [5, 3, 8, 4, 1]. Bubble sort ise aise sort karega: 1. Pehle element (5) ko second element (3) se compare kiya. 5 bada ah, toh swap ho gaya. List ab [3, 5, 8, 4, 1] he. 2. Next element (5) ko (8) se compare kiya. 5 chhota hai, toh koi change nahi. List wahi rahi [3, 5, 8, 4, 1]. 3. Next element (8) ko (4) se compare kiya. 8 bada hai, toh swap ho gaya. List ab [3, 5, 4, 8, 1] hai. 4. Next element (8) ko (1) se compare kiya. 8 bada hai, toh swap ho gaya. List ab [3, 5, 4, 1, 8] hai. 5. Ab hum end tak pahunch gaye, toh phir se start se loop chalega. Ye steps tab tak repeat honge jab tak puri list sorted na ho jaye. 6. Kuch or passes ke baad, list eventually [1, 3, 4, 5, 8] ban jayegi, jo ki sorted list hai. Ye bas ek example tha. Iske alawa Insertion Sort aur Selection Sort jaise aur bhi algorithms hote hain.

instruction: Three real numbers a, b, aur c equations a+b+c=2, ab+ac+bc=-7 aur abc=-14 satisfy karte hain. In teeno mein se sabse bada number kaunsa hai? Answer simplest radical form mein dena.
output: Isko solve karne ke liye Vieta's formulas use karenge. Given values se hum keh sakte hain ki a, b, aur c is cubic equation ke solutions hain: x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x + 14 = 0. Ab isko group karke factor karte hain: x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x + 14 = 0 = (x^3 - 7x) - (2x^2 - 14) = x(x^2 - 7) - 2(x^2 - 7) = (x-2)(x^2 - 7) Toh equation ke three solutions hue x=2, x=sqrt(7), aur x=-sqrt(7). Inme se sabse bada number sqrt(7) hai.

instruction: Hamara hero Teemo ek enemy Ashe ko poison attacks se attack kar raha hai! Jab Teemo Ashe par attack karta hai, toh Ashe exactly 'duration' seconds ke liye poison ho jati hai. Agar technically kahein toh, second 't' par attack hone ka matlab hai ki Ashe [t, t + duration - 1] inclusive time interval tak poisoned rahegi. Agar Teemo poison effect khatam hone se pehle fir se attack karta hai, toh timer reset ho jayega aur naye attack ke baad duration seconds tak poison effect rahega. Aapko ek non-decreasing integer array 'timeSeries' diya gaya hai, jahan timeSeries[i] batata hai ki Teemo ne second timeSeries[i] par Ashe ko attack kiya, aur ek integer 'duration' diya gaya hai. Total kitne seconds tak Ashe poisoned rahi, wo return karo.
output: Is problem ko solve karne ke liye, hum timeSeries par iterate karenge ar current aur previous attack times ka difference nikaalenge. Agar difference duration se kam hai, toh poison effect sirf us difference time tak rahega. Agar difference duration se zyada ya equal he, toh poison effect full duration tak chalega. Bas saari poison effect durations ko add kar do aur total seconds mil jayenge. Code ye raha: ``` def findPoisonedDuration(timeSeries, duration): total_duration = 0 for i in range(len(timeSeries)): if i == 0: total_duration += duration else: diff = timeSeries[i] - timeSeries[i-1] total_duration += min(diff, duration) return total_duration ``` Example usage: ``` timeSeries = [1,4,7,10] duration = 3 print(findPoisonedDuration(timeSeries, duration)) # Output: 9 ``` Is example mein, Teemo ne Ashe ko seconds 1, 4, 7, aur 10 par attack kiya. Poison effect har baar 3 seconds tak rehta hai. Second 1 par, poison full 3 seconds tak chalta hai. Second 4 par, fir 3 seconds (second 6 tak). Second 7 par, fir 3 seconds (second 9 tak). Aur second 10 par, fir se full 3 seconds. Toh total poison duration 9 seconds hui.

instruction: Kisi element x ka next greater element wo pehla element hota hai jo x ke right side mein ho aur x se bada ho. Aapko do distinct 0-indexed integer arrays 'nums1' aur 'nums2' diye gaye hain, jahan nums1, nums2 ka ek subset hai. Har 0 <= i < nums1.length ke liye, aisa index j dhoondo ki nums1[i] == nums2[j] ho, aur fir nums2[j] ka next greater element nums2 mein find karo. Agar koi next greater element nahi hai, toh answer -1 hoga. Ek array 'ans' return karo jiski length nums1.length ho aur ans[i] upar bataye gaye next greater element ko represent kare.
output: Is problem ko solve karne ke liye, hum nums2 ko right to left iterate karenge aur 1 stack use karenge taaki har element ka next greater element track ho sake. Fir nums1 ke har element ke liye nums2 mein uska index dhoond kar stack se corresponding value nikaal lenge. Agar next greater nahi mila, toh -1 return karenge. Python code ye raha: ``` def nextGreaterElement(nums1, nums2): stack = [] next_greater = {} for num in nums2[::-1]: while stack and num >= stack[-1]: # stack se un elements ko nikalo jo num se chhote hain stack.pop() if stack: next_greater[num] = stack[-1] else: next_greater[num] = -1 stack.append(num) ans = [] for num in nums1: ans.append(next_greater[num]) return ans ```

instruction: Data points ko classify karne ke liye K-nearest neighbors algorithm use karo. Iska ek python program likho. Data points: [[1,2],[2,4],[2,3],[3,5],[3,1],[5,5],[5,3],[6,1],[6,2],[6,4]]
output: Haan, ye raha Python implementation KNN algorithm ka, isse data points do categories (0 ya 1) mein classify ho jayenge: ``` import math def knn(data, query, k, distance_fn, choice_fn): neighbor_distances_and_indices = [] # Query point aur saare data points ke beech ka distance calculate karo for index, point in enumerate(data): distance = distance_fn(point, query) neighbor_distances_and_indices.append((distance, index)) # Distances ko ascending order mein sort karo sorted_neighbor_distances_and_indices = sorted(neighbor_distances_and_indices) # Pehle k neighbors select karo k_nearest_distances_and_indices = sorted_neighbor_distances_and_indices[:k] # k nearest neighbors ke labels nikaalo k_nearest_labels = [data[i][-1] for distance, i in k_nearest_distances_and_indices] # Final label determine karne ke liye choice function use karo return choice_fn(k_nearest_labels) def euclidean_distance(point1, point2): sum_squared_distance = 0 for i in range(len(point1)): sum_squared_distance += math.pow(point1[i] - point2[i], 2) return math.sqrt(sum_squared_distance) def majority_vote(labels): vote_counts = {} for label in labels: vote_counts[label] = vote_counts.get(label, 0) + 1 winner = max(vote_counts.items(), key=lambda x:x[1])[0] return winner # Example usage: data = [[1,2,1],[2,4,1],[2,3,1],[3,5,1],[3,1,0],[5,5,0],[5,3,0],[6,1,0],[6,2,0],[6,4,0]] query = [4,4] k = 3 prediction = knn(data, query, k, distance_fn=euclidean_distance, choice_fn=majority_vote) print(prediction) ``` Is example mein, humne distance function ke liye Euclidean distance aur choice function ke liye majority voting use kiya hai. Program ka output 1 aayega, kyunki query point [4,4] ke zyadatar nearest neighbors ka label 1 hai.

instruction: Ek SQL query likho jo saare customers ke naam aur unhone jo product kharide hain, wo return kare.
output: Ye le query, isse kaam ho jayega: ``` SELECT customers.name, products.name AS product FROM customers INNER JOIN orders ON customers.id = orders.customer_id INNER JOIN order_items ON orders.id = order_items.order_id INNER JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.id ``` Isme assume kiya hai ki `customers`, `orders`, `order_items`, aur `products` naam ke tables hain, jisme ye columns hain: - `customers` table mein `id` (unique ID) aur `name` column hai. - `orders` table mein `id` aur `customer_id` (jisne order place kiya) hai. - `order_items` table mein `order_id` aur `product_id` hai. - `products` table mein `id` aur `name` column ah. Query pehle `customers` aur `orders` tables ke beech `INNER JOIN` karti hai, jahan `customer_id` match hota hai. Phir result ko `order_items` ke saath join karti hai `order_id` ke basis pe. Last mein, `products` table ko join kiya gaya hai `product_id` use karke. Result mein customer ka `name` ar product ka `name` aayega. `AS` keyword use karke `products.name` column ko rename karke `product` kar diya hai.

Basically, in techniques aur tools ka combination ek robust system bana dega jo concise or informative summaries generate kar sake.

instruction: 4x^2 + ax + 8x + 9 = 0 is equation ke liye 'a' ki do values hain jiske liye x ka sirf ek solution aata hai. Un values ka sum kya hoga?
output: Pehle given quadratic equation se start karte hain: 4x^2 + ax + 8x + 9 = 0 Isko simplify karke aise likh sakte hain: 4x^2 + (a + 8)x + 9 = 0 Agar x ka sirf 1 solution chahiye, toh quadratic ka discriminant zero hona chahiye: (a + 8)^2 - 4 * 4 * 9 = 0 Isko expand karenge toh milega: a^2 + 16a - 80 = 0 Ab Vieta's formulas ke hisaab se, roots ka sum linear term ke coefficient ka opposite hota hai, jo yahan -16 hai. Toh, 'a' ki un values ka sum -16 hoga jiske liye quadratic ka sirf ek solution hai.

instruction: Is problem ke liye C++ mein solution likho: Given the root of a binary search tree (BST) with duplicates, return all the mode(s) (i.e., the most frequently occurred element) in it. If the tree has more than one mode, return them in any order. Assume a BST is defined as follows: - The left subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys less than or equal to the node's key. - The right subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys greater than or equal to the node's key. - Both the left and right subtrees must also be binary search trees.
output: Ye raha is problem ka ek possible solution: ```cpp class Solution { public: vector<int> findMode(TreeNode* root) { unordered_map<int, int> freq; // frequency map int maxFreq = 0; // maximum frequency so far traverse(root, freq, maxFreq); // traverse the tree and update the frequency map vector<int> modes; // output vector for (auto [key, count] : freq) { // loop over the frequency map if (count == maxFreq) { // if the current key has maximum frequency modes.push_back(key); // add it to the output } } return modes; } private: void traverse(TreeNode* root, unordered_map<int, int>& freq, int& maxFreq) { if (!root) return; traverse(root->left, freq, maxFreq); maxFreq = max(maxFreq, ++freq[root->val]); // update the frequency of the current node traverse(root->right, freq, maxFreq); } }; ``` `findMode` function `TreeNode*` argument leta hai aur `vector<int>` return karta hai jisme BST ke mode(s) hote hain. Ye ek empty frequency map (`freq`) aur ek `maxFreq` variable initialize karta hai. Phir `traverse` function call karke tree ko inorder traverse karta hai aur frequency map aur max frequency update karta hai. `traverse` ek helper function ah jo `TreeNode*`, frequency map ka reference, aur `maxFreq` ka reference leta hai. Ye inorder traversal perform karke har node ki frequency update karta he. Last mein, `findMode` function frequency map pe loop chalata hai aur jin keys ki frequency `maxFreq` ke equal hai, unhe `modes` vector mein daal kar return kar deta hai. Loop ko simple rakhne ke liye structured bindings (`auto [key, count]`) use kiye hain.

instruction: Ek integer 'num' diya hai, uska base 7 representation string mein return karna hai. C++ mein ye solution kaise kaam karega?
output: Dekho, ye akk C++ solution hai jo recursion use karke `num` ko base-7 mein convert karta hai: ``` #include <string> using namespace std; class Solution { public: string convertToBase7(int num) { if (num < 0) { return "-" + convertToBase7(-num); } else if (num < 7) { return to_string(num); } else { return convertToBase7(num / 7) + to_string(num % 7); } } }; ``` `convertToBase7` function integer `num` leta hai aur uska base-7 string return karta hai. Agar `num` negative hai, toh hum uski absolute value convert karke aage "-" sign laga dete hain. Agar `num` 7 se chota hai, toh bas `to_string` use karke usko return kar dete hain. Warna, hum `convertToBase7` ko recursively call karte hain `num / 7` ke saath, or result ke end mein remainder (`num % 7`) append kar dete hain. Recursion tab rukta hai jab `num` 7 se chota ho jata hai, toh function eventually correct base-7 representation return kar dega.

instruction: Ek regular expression likho jo validate kare ki phone number 10 digits ka ho aur 7 se start ho.
output: 10 digits aur 7 se start hone wale phone number ke liye regex hoga `^7\d{9}$`. Simple explanation: - `^` matlab string ka start. - `7` matlab pehla character 7 hona chahiye. - `\d` matlab koi bhi digit (0-9). - `{9}` matlab pichla wala digit 9 baar repeat hona chahiye. - `$` matlab string ka end. Is regex se wo saare numbers validate ho jayenge jo exactly 10 digits ke hain aur 7 se start hote hain.

instruction: Aapko size 'n' ka ek integer array 'score' diya gaya hai, jahan score[i] ith athlete ka score hai. Saare scores unique hain. Athletes ko unke scores ke basis par place kiya gaya hai, jahan 1st place wale ka score highest hai, 2nd place wale ka 2nd highest, aur aise hi aage. Rank aise decide hogi: - 1st place athlete ka rank "Gold Medal" hai. - 2nd place athlete ka rank "Silver Medal" hai. - 3rd place athlete ka rank "Bronze Medal" hai. - 4th place se nth place tak, unka rank unka placement number hoga (yani xth place wale ka rank "x" hoga). Ek array 'answer' return karo jahan answer[i] ith athlete ka rank ho.
output: Sabse pehle ek empty dictionary bana lo jisme athlete ka score key ho aur rank value. Phir array ko descending order mein sort karke iterate karo. Pehle 3 athletes ko unke respective medals assign kar do. Baaki athletes ke liye unka placement number hi rank hoga. Last mein, dictionary use karke answer array populate kar lo. Code ye raha: ``` def findRanks(score): rank_dict = {} for i in range(len(score)): rank_dict[score[i]] = 0 sorted_scores = sorted(score, reverse=True) for i in range(len(sorted_scores)): if i == 0: rank_dict[sorted_scores[i]] = "Gold Medal" elif i == 1: rank_dict[sorted_scores[i]] = "Silver Medal" elif i == 2: rank_dict[sorted_scores[i]] = "Bronze Medal" else: rank_dict[sorted_scores[i]] = str(i+1) answer = [] for i in range(len(score)): answer.append(rank_dict[score[i]]) return answer ``` Phir aap `findRanks` ko aise call kar sakte ho: ``` scores = [10, 5, 15, 20, 25] ranks = findRanks(scores) print(ranks) # outputs ["Silver Medal", "5", "Bronze Medal", "Gold Medal", "1"] ```

instruction: Do vectors ke beech squared differences ka sum calculate karo. Vector x: [10, 8, 5] Vector y: [5, 6, 2]
output: Do vectors ke squared differences nikalne ke liye, corresponding elements ko subtract karo, result ko square karo, aur phir saare squared differences ko add kar do. Calculation aise hogi: - Pehle element ke liye: (10 - 5)^2 = 5^2 = 25 - Doosre element ke liye: (8 - 6)^2 = 2^2 = 4 - Teesre element ke liye: (5 - 2)^2 = 3^2 = 9 Toh vector x aur y ke squared differences ka total sum hai: 25 + 4 + 9 = 38

instruction: Perfect number wo positive integer hota hai jo apne positive divisors ke sum ke barabar ho, bas us number ko exclude karke. Integer x ka divisor wo hota hai jo x ko evenly divide kar sake. Ek integer n diya gaya hai, return karo true agar n ek perfect number hai, nahi toh return karo false.
output: Agar check karna hai ki n perfect number hai ya nahi, ta hum uske saare positive divisors ka sum nikaal kar check kar sakte hain ki wo n ke equal hai ya nahi. Ye raha iska Python code: ``` def isPerfectNumber(n): if n <= 0: return False divisors_sum = 0 for i in range(1, n): if n % i == 0: divisors_sum += i return divisors_sum == n ``` Sabse pehle hum check karte hain ki n zero ya usse kam toh nahi hai, kyunki aise case mein wo perfect number nahi ho sakta. Phir hum ek variable `divisors_sum` ko zero set karte hain aur 1 se lekar n-1 tak loop chalate hain. Har `i` ke liye hum check karte hain ki kya wo n ka divisor hai (n % i == 0). Agar hai, toh use `divisors_sum` mein add kar dete hain. Last mein, bas ye check karna hai ki `divisors_sum` n ke barabar hai ya nahi. Agar hai toh True, nah toh False.

instruction: Do poems ko compare karte hue ek essay likho. "A Red, Red Rose” by Robert Burns aur “The New Colossus” by Emma Lazarus
output: Dekh, Robert Burns ki “A Red, Red Rose” aur Emma Lazarus ki “The New Colossus” dono hi kaafi powerful poems hain jo deep emotions dikhati hain. Dono verse form mein hain aur strong feelings convey karti hain, par inka subject, tone aur structure kaafi alag hai. Subject matter ki baat karein toh “A Red, Red Rose” ek love poem hai. Burns ne romantic imagery use karke apne pyaar ki intensity dikhayi he. Poori poem metaphors ar similes se bhari hai, jaise pyaar ko “newly sprung” rose ya ek “sweetly played” melody se compare karna. Doosri taraf, “The New Colossus” Statue of Liberty aur immigrants ke welcome ke baare mein hai. Lazarus ne “mighty woman with a torch” wali image use ki ah ye dikhane ke liye ki America un logo ke liye hope aur opportunity he jo poverty aur persecution se bhaag kar aa rahe hain. Tone bhi bilkul different hai. “A Red, Red Rose” ekdum romantic aur sentimental hai. Burns kehta hai ki uska pyaar tab tak rahega “till a’ the seas gang dry” aur “till the rocks melt wi’ the sun.” Par “The New Colossus” proud aur defiant hai. Lazarus ne strong language use ki hai Statue of Liberty ki strength dikhane ke liye. Wo batati hai ki statue ka “beacon-hand” poori duniya ko welcome karta hai. Structure dekhein ta dono traditional forms follow karte hain. “A Red, Red Rose” simple four-line stanza aur regular rhyme scheme mein ah, jabki “The New Colossus” ek sonnet hai. Burns ne simple structure rakha hai emotions ke liye, par Lazarus ne complex sonnet form use kiya hai America ke role ko explore karne ke liye. In short, dono poems strong emotions aur imagery use karti hain, par Burns ki poem ek romantic love letter hai, jabki Lazarus ki poem ek national symbol ki taqat dikhati ah.

instruction: "The New Colossus" aur "Sonnet 19" mein freedom ke themes ko compare karo. "The New Colossus" by Emma Lazarus aur "Sonnet 19" by William Shakespeare
output: Dekho, freedom ka concept dono poems mein kaafi alag tarike se dikhaya gaya hai. Dhyan se samajhna. "The New Colossus" mein freedom ko ek gift ki tarah dikhaya gaya hai jo un logo ke liye hai jo thake hue hain, gareeb hain, ya jinhe apna ghar chhodna pada. Emma Lazarus ne Statue of Liberty ko ek hope ke beacon ki tarah pesh kiya hai un logo ke liye jo azadi ki talash mein duniya bhar se aate hain. Poem mein goddess torch pakde hue hai, jo immigrants ko opportunity aur freedom ki nayi zameen par welcome kar rahi hai. Doosri taraf, Shakespeare ki "Sonnet 19" mein freedom ka matlab hai waqt (time) ki barbadi se azadi. Speaker waqt se request karta hai ki wo us person ki jawani aur beauty ko khatam na kare jiske baare mein wo likh raha hai. Halanki use pata hai ki time ko roka nahi ja sakta, par wo apni poetry ke zariye us beauty ko preserve karke ek tarah ki freedom offer karta hai. Conclusion ye hai ki jahan "The New Colossus" freedom ko ek physical state aur behtar zindagi ki opportunity maanta hai, wahin "Sonnet 19" freedom ko poetic expression ke zariye waqt ki pabandiyon se azadi ke roop mein dekhta hai.

instruction: Ek specific input ke basis par physics story problem generate karo. Ek cylindrical tube jiska radius 2 cm hai, usme air 0.5 kg/sec ki speed se flow ho rahi hai.
output: Jenny ek experiment kar rahi hai air density check karne ke liye. Tube ka radius 2 cm hai ar mass flow rate 0.5 kg/sec hai. Agar cross sectional area 0.001256 square meters hai, toh air ki density (kg/m^3) calculate karo. Logic simple hai: density $\rho = m/V$ hota hai. Per second flow hone wala volume = mass flow rate / density. Yahan volume flow rate 0.5 / density hoga. Cross sectional area 0.001256 $m^2$ hai, toh air column ki length (ya speed) nikalne ke liye volume flow rate ko area se divide karo. Finally, mass flow rate ko (area $\times$ speed) se divide karke density mil jayegi: 0.5 / (0.001256 $\times$ air speed).

instruction: Kuch musical notes diye gaye hain, in par ek 500-word story likho. * C major * D minor * F major * G major
output: Midnight ka time tha aur concert hall ek dum bhara hua tha. Orchestra ek aisi symphony baja raha tha jo emotional notes se bhari hui thi. Unme C major, D minor, F major aur G major aise chamak rahe the jaise koi heere hon, ek aisi kahani bunte hue jisne sabka dil chhu liya. Kahani shuru hui C major ki bright aur cheerful sound se, jisne mahool mein ek khushi bhar di. Ek chota ladka, jiske dil mein dher saare sapne aur imagination thi, sadak par chal raha tha. Uski aankhon mein ek chamak thi aur wo apne aas-paas ki duniya ko dekh kar bahut excited tha. Use lag raha tha ki life mein kitni saari possibilities hain. Par jaise hi wo ek andheri gali mein muda, music change ho gaya aur D minor ki udaas dhun bajne lagi. Ladke ki smile gayab ho gayi. Ab use duniya alag dikh rahi thi. Shadows use gherne lagin or uske dil mein akk ajeeb si sadness aur despair bhar gaya. Wo thaka hua aur udaas chalta raha, tabhi concert hall mein F major ki goonj sunayi di. Usi pal, badalon ke beech se suraj nikla aur ladke ne upar dekha, uski aankhon mein phir se hope dikhne lagi. Use apne chehre par garmahat feel hui aur use ehsas hua ki chahe kuch bhi ho, use aage badhte rehna hai, 1 bright future ki taraf. Aur phir, music ek dum se tez hua aur G major burst hua, jisse poore hall mein victory aur triumph ki feeling aa gayi. Ladka andheron se bahar nikal kar bhaga, uska dil excitement se dhadak raha tha aur wo duniya ki beauty ko phir se dekh pa raha tha. Concert khatam hua, last notes raat ke sannate mein kho gaye, par wo kahani audience ke dilon mein reh gayi. Ye ek tale thi hope aur dreams ki, andheron se ladkar light dhoondhne ki. Isne sikhaya ki life chahe kitne bhi challenges throw kare, humein hamesha aage badhte rehna chahiye. Jab log hall se bahar nikle, wo abhi bhi us symphony ko gunguna rahe the. C major ne khushi di, D minor ne dukh, F major ne umeed or G major ne jeet. In sab notes ne milkar ek aisi story banayi jo hamesha yaad rahegi.

instruction: Kuch inputs diye gaye hain, ek strategy banao jisse company aur customers ke beech trust build ho sake. 1. Transparency 2. Respect of customers 3. High service quality
output: Sun, company aur customers ke beech trust build karne ke liye ye strategy sahi rahegi, bas in teen points par focus karna hai: 1. Transparency: Company ko apne communication mein ekdum open aur honest rehna chahiye. Policies ke baare mein pehle se batao, customer queries ka timely ar clear response do, aur agar koi mistake ho jaye toh use maan lo. Saath hi, company ki performance aur changes ke regular updates dete raho. 2. Respect for customers: Customers ki opinions aur feedback ko value karo. Unki problems ko dhyan se suno or solve karo, isse unhe lagega ki company unki respect karti he. Customer service team ko properly train karo taaki wo sabse kindness aur respect se baat karein. 3. High service quality: Hamesha customer expectations se zyada deliver karne ki koshish karo. Products ki quality top-notch honi chahiye aur support system fast aur responsive hona chahiye. Employees ki regular training karwao taaki service quality maintain rahe. Basically, agar transparency rakhi, respect di aur high-quality service provide ki, toh customers ka trust aur loyalty apne aap badh jayegi aur ek long-term relationship ban jayega.

instruction: Ek Software Engineer ko apni nayi job ke pehle mahine mein kaunsi 3 cheezein karni chahiye?
output: Dekho, pehle mahine mein zyada panic karne ki zaroorat nahi hai, bas ye 3 cheezein dhyan se follow karo: 1. Company culture aur processes ko samjho: Time nikalo aur ye dekho ki company kaam kaise karti hai, unka work ethic kya hai aur development methodology (jaise Agile ya Scrum) kya follow ho rahi hai. Jab tum values aur goals samajh loge, tabhi team mein fit ho paoge aur sahi contribute kar paoge. 2. Team se connect karo aur help maangne mein sharmao mat: Apne manager, fellow developers aur baaki coworkers se interact karo. Ache working relations banane se collaboration easy ho jata hai. Aur haan, agar kuch samajh nahi aa raha toh turant pucho; sharmaoge toh productivity giregi aur seekhne mein time lagega. 3. Codebase aur tools se familiar ho jao: Pehle mahine ka main goal hona chahiye codebase ko samajhna. Architecture kya hai, kaunsi languages aur frameworks use ho rahe hain, aur collaboration tools (jaise Git, Jira) kaise kaam kar rahe hain, ye sab seekho. Jab tum codebase samajh jaoge, tabhi meaningful contributions kar paoge.

instruction: Is team ka collaboration style identify karo - har team member apne task pe khud kaam karta hai par overall project mein contribute karta hai.

instruction: Is equation ka antiderivative nikalo aur jitna ho sake simplify karo. 5x^2 + 3x
output: 5x^2 + 3x ka antiderivative nikalne ke liye bas is function ko x ke respect mein integrate karna ha. Matlab humein ek aisi function chahiye jiska derivative original function ke barabar ho. 5x^2 ka antiderivative (5/3)x^3 hoga. Aur 3x ka antiderivative (3/2)x^2 hoga. Finally, humein integration constant add karna hoga, jise usually "C" se represent karte hain. Toh final antiderivative hai: (5/3)x^3 + (3/2)x^2 + C

instruction: Is production log ko process karo, timestamps extract karo aur unka difference minutes mein batao. Started at 14:30 Completed at 16:45

Difference calculate karne ke liye: Sabse pehle dono timestamps ko minutes mein convert karte hain: - `14:30` ko convert karne ke liye hours ko 60 se multiply karke minutes add karo: `(14 * 60) + 30 = 870` - `16:45` ke liye bhi same: `(16 * 60) + 45 = 1005` Ab end time mein se start time subtract karo: - `1005 - 870 = 135 minutes` Toh total difference 135 minutes hai, yaani 2 hours and 15 minutes.

instruction: Is programming question ka answer do: Static aur dynamic array mein kya difference hota hai?
output: Static array wo hota hai jiska size fixed hota hai. Iska matlab hai ki usme kitne elements aayenge ye declaration ke time hi decide ho jata hai aur memory compile-time pe allocate hoti hai. Runtime pe tum iska size change nhiii kar sakte. Static arrays ka memory footprint kam hota hai aur elements access karna faster hota ah kyunki size aur memory location compile-time pe hi pata hoti hai. Dusri taraf, dynamic array shuruat mein 1 specific size ke saath banta ah, lekin runtime pe iska size change kiya ja sakta hai jab elements add ya remove hote hain. Iski memory runtime pe allocate hoti hai or zaroorat ke hisaab se grow ya shrink ho sakti hai. Is wajah se dynamic arrays zyada flexible hote hain kyunki tumhe pehle se bada size declare karne ki zaroorat nahi padti. Halanki, inka memory footprint zyada hota hai aur access time slow ho sakta hai, kyunki memory location compile-time pe fixed nahi hoti aur array grow hone par reallocate karni pad sakti hai.

instruction: Instant ice cream ke naye ad campaign ki effectiveness measure karne ke liye ek experiment propose karo.
input: The new advertising campaign is for a brand of instant ice cream.
output: Simple sa A/B test karo. Do groups banao: ek jisko ad dikhega (treatment) or ek jisko nahi (control). Steps ye hain: 1. Target market se sample lo ar randomly do groups mein divide karo. Demographics same hone chahiye. 2. Treatment group ko TV, billboards, online ads dikhao. Control group ko kuch nahi. 3. Ek mahine tak dono groups ki sales track karo. 4. Data compare karo. Agar treatment group ki sales zyada badhi, toh ad hit hai. Warna flop. 5. Treatment group se feedback lo ki unhe campaign kaisa laga. 6. Weather, holidays ya competitors jaise external factors ka bhi dhyan rakhna.

instruction: Ethanol ki volatility measure karne ke liye ek scientific experiment design karo.
output: Ethanol ki volatility ke liye Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) measure karna hoga. RVP jitna high, fuel utna volatile. Ye lo setup: Materials: Temperature-controlled water bath, pressure gauge wala sample container, Ethanol, thermometer, aur stopwatch. Procedure: 1. Water bath ko 37.8 degrees Celsius pe set karo (standard temp). 2. Container mein ethanol daalo. 3. Seal karke water bath mein rakh do. 4. 5 mins wait karo taaki temperature stabilize ho jaye. 5. Thermometer se check karo ki temp 37.8 hi aahe. 6. Pressure gauge ki reading note karo. 7. Average nikalne ke liye ye process 3 baar repeat karo. Is value ko doosre fuels ke RVP se compare karke volatility pata chal jayegi.

instruction: Problem diagnose karo aur solution batao: "Mera laptop slow chal raha hai aur aksar crash ho jata hai."
output: Lagta hai performance issues hain, iske kai reasons ho sakte hain. Ye try karo: 1. Low disk space: Agar hard drive full hai toh laptop slow ho jayega. Faltu files delete karo aur recycle bin khaali karo. 2. Too many programs: Ek saath bahut saare apps open rakhne se RAM full ho jati hai. Unused programs band karo ya RAM upgrade karwa lo. 3. Malware ya Virus: Virus ki wajah se bhi system slow hota hai. Updated antivirus se full scan run karo. 4. Fragmented hard drive: Files alag-alag jagah store hone se access slow ho jata hai. Disk defragmenter chala lo. 5. Outdated drivers: Saare drivers update rakho, kyunki purane drivers performance kharab karte hain. Ek-ek karke try karo. Agar phir bhi nahi chala, toh hardware issue ho sakta hai, kisi technician ko dikha lo.

instruction: Digital marketing campaign successful banane ke liye 5 critical success factors ki list banao.

instruction: COVID-19 safety measures follow karna kyun zaroori hai, ispe ek article likho.
output: COVID-19 Safety Measures Follow Karna Kyun Zaroori Hai COVID-19, jise coronavirus bhi kehte hain, ek bahut infectious virus hai jisne poori duniya hila di. Lockdowns lag gaye, healthcare systems collapse hone lage, or logo ko apni lifestyle badalni padi taaki virus na phaile. Par kuch log aise hain jinhe lagta hai ki unhe kuch nahi hoga aur wo safety rules follow nahi karte. Is article mein hum dekhenge ki ye measures follow karna kyun crucial hai. Pehli baat, COVID-19 ek naya virus hai jo bahut jaldi phaileta hai. Ye hawa mein droplets ke zariye, jab koi infected insaan baat karta hai, khasta hai ya cheenkta hai, toh spread ho sakta hai. Iske alawa, contaminated surfaces aur objects se bhi ye phaileta hai. Virus kuch surfaces pe 72 hours tak survive kar sakta hai, matlab bina pata chale kisi ko bhi infection ho sakta hai. Isliye masks pehenna aur haath dhona bahut zaroori hai. Doosri baat, zyada tar logo mein symptoms mild hote hain, par serious complications ka risk kaafi zyada hota hai. Isse severe respiratory problems aur kabhi kabhi organ failure bhi ho sakta hai. Long-term health pe bhi iska bura asar padta hai. Isliye social distancing, bheed se bachna, aur elderly logo ya pre-existing conditions wale logo ka khayal rakhna bahut zaroori hai. Finally, safety measures follow karne se healthcare system ka load kam hota hai. Pandemic ki wajah se hospitals pe bahut pressure aa gaya aahe. Patients ki sankhya itni badh gayi ki beds, ventilators aur PPE kits ki kami ho gayi. Agar hum safety follow karenge, toh virus slow phailega aur zaroorat mando ko behtar treatment mil payega. Conclusion ye hai ki COVID-19 safety measures follow karne ke peeche bahut solid reasons hain. Rules na manne se sirf hum nahi, balki dusre bhi risk mein aate hain. Humein milkar is virus ko rokna hoga. Safety follow karke hum isse lad sakte hain.

instruction: Ek program banao jo web page se data collect kare. URL of the web page: https://www.example.com
output: Ye lo code, isse kaam ho jayega: ```python import requests from bs4 import BeautifulSoup url = "https://www.example.com" response = requests.get(url) if response.status_code == 200: page_content = response.content soup = BeautifulSoup(page_content, 'html.parser') # Now we can collect the data from the page using 'soup' object. # For example, to get all the links on this page: links = [] for link in soup.find_all('a'): links.append(link.get('href')) print(links) else: print("An error occurred while fetching the web page") ``` Bas requests aur bs4 install kar lena.

instruction: Ye parameters use karke ek algorithm design karo. Ek integers ki list aur target sum diya hai, toh woh saare combinations find karo jo target sum tak pahunche.
output: Is problem ko solve karne ke liye backtracking best rahega, kyunki isse saare possible combinations efficiently mil jate hain. ```python def combinationSum(candidates, target): result = [] backtrack(result, [], candidates, target, 0) return result def backtrack(result, temp, candidates, remain, start): if remain < 0: return elif remain == 0: result.append(temp[:]) else: for i in range(start, len(candidates)): temp.append(candidates[i]) backtrack(result, temp, candidates, remain-candidates[i], i) temp.pop() ``` Ye algorithm `candidates` (integers ki list) aur `target` sum ko input leta hai. Output mein ye lists ki akk list return karta hai, jahan har list ek valid combination hoti hai. `backtrack` function ek recursive function hai jisme ye parameters hain: - `result`: Yahan saare final combinations store hote hain. - `temp`: Current combination ko track karne ke liye temporary list. - `candidates`: Woh integers jinhe hum consider kar rahe hain. - `remain`: Jitna sum aur chahiye. - `start`: Candidates list ka starting index. Sabse pehle function check karta hai ki `remain` 0 se kam toh nahi ho gaya, agar haan ta return kar jata hai kyunki koi valid combination nahi milega. Agar `remain` 0 ha, iska matlab combination mil gaya aur usko `result` mein add kar dete hain. Warna, function `start` index se loop chalata hai, candidate ko `temp` mein daalta hai or firse `backtrack` call karta hai updated sum aur index ke saath. Jab recursive call khatam hoti hai, toh woh candidate `temp` se pop kar diya jata hai. Bas `combinationSum` function ko `candidates` aur `target` pass karo, woh result initialize karke `backtrack` call kar dega.

instruction: Hum ek word mein capitals ka usage tab sahi maante hain jab inme se koi ek case ho: - Word ke saare letters capitals hon, jaise "USA". - Word ka ek bhi letter capital na ho, jaise "leetcode". - Sirf pehla letter capital ho, jaise "Google". Ek string 'word' di gayi hai, return karo true agar capitals ka usage sahi hai.
output: Regex use kar lo, sorted hai. Python code ye raha: ```python import re def detectCapitalUse(word: str) -> bool: return re.fullmatch('[A-Z]*|.[a-z]*', word) is not None or re.fullmatch('[A-Z][a-z]*', word) is not None ``` Agar capitals sahi hain toh True aayega, warna False.

instruction: Is 3D array ko 1D array mein convert karo [[[1, 2], [3, 4]], [[5, 6], [7, 8]]]
output: 3D array ko 1D mein convert karne ke liye ye try karo: Pehla tareeka simple iteration hai: ```python arr = [[[1, 2], [3, 4]], [[5, 6], [7, 8]]] flat_list = [] for sublist in arr: for subsublist in sublist: for item in subsublist: flat_list.append(item) print(flat_list) ``` Doosra shortcut list comprehension hai: ```python arr = [[[1, 2], [3, 4]], [[5, 6], [7, 8]]] flat_list = [item for sublist in arr for subsublist in sublist for item in subsublist] print(flat_list) ``` Dono se same result aayega: `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]`

instruction: Java mein solution likho. Do strings 'a' aur 'b' di gayi hain, return karo longest uncommon subsequence ki length. Agar koi longest uncommon subsequence nahi hai, toh -1 return karo. Uncommon subsequence wo string hoti hai jo ek string ka subsequence ho par doosre ka nahi. Subsequence wo string hoti hai jo original string se characters delete karke banayi ja sake. - Example: "abc", "aebdc" ka subsequence hai kyunki "aebdc" se characters delete karke "abc" mil sakta hai.
output: Java mein solution ye raha: ```java public int findLUSlength(String a, String b) { if (a.equals(b)) { return -1; } else { return Math.max(a.length(), b.length()); } } ``` Explanation: - Sabse pehle `equals` method se check karo ki dono strings same hain ya nahi. Agar same hain, toh koi uncommon subsequence nahi hoga, isliye -1 return kar do. - Agar same nahi hain, toh jo string lambi hogi wahi longest uncommon subsequence hogi. `Math.max` use karke max length nikal lo. - Ye method integer value return kar dega.

instruction: Is cause ke liye ek argument banao ki ye true kyun hai. Current pandemic climate change ki wajah se hua hai.
output: Kafi evidence mil raha hai ki current pandemic ka connection climate change se ho sakta hai. Climate change ki wajah se nature badal raha hai, animals ke habitats shift ho rahe hain aur ecosystems disrupt ho rahe hain. Isse animals aur humans ke beech interactions badh gaye hain, jis se viruses naye regions aur hosts tak pahunch gaye hain, jinme humans bhi shamil hain. Duniya ke kai hisson mein temperature badhne se precipitation ka timing aur intensity change hui ha, kahin paani kam ho gaya toh kahin floods aa gaye. Iska asar animals ke behavior pe padta hai aur humans se contact hone ke chances badh jaate hain. Jab habitats rehne layak nahi bache, toh animals khane ar shelter ke liye naye areas mein migrate karne lage. Is displacement ki wajah se wo humans ke close aa gaye, jis se COVID-19 jaise diseases spread hone ka risk badh gaya. Plus, climate change deforestation, urbanization aur wildlife trade jaise factors ko aur kharab karta ha. Ye sab zoonotic diseases ka risk badhate hain. Overall, pandemics ke piche kai reasons ho sakte hain, par climate change akk bada concern hai. Ecosystems ko badal kar aur animals ki movement badha kar, ye pathogens ko species barrier cross karne mein help kar raha hai aur human populations ko affect kar raha hai.

instruction: Dijkstra's algorithm use karke do cities ke beech shortest path nikalo. New York aur San Francisco
output: Dijkstra's algorithm basically ek weighted graph mein do nodes ke beech shortest path nikalne ke liye use hota hai, jahan weight distance ko represent karta ha. Is case mein, hum New York aur San Francisco ke beech shortest path nikalne ke liye isse use kar sakte hain. Maan lo humare paas USA ka ek map-graph hai jahan edges highways hain ar weights distances hain, toh process aise chalega: 1. New York se start karenge, use distance 0 assign karenge aur baaki saari cities ko infinity. 2. New York ko current city maan kar uske saare outgoing edges check karenge aur neighboring cities ki tentative distances update karenge. 3. Jis city ki tentative distance sabse kam hogi, use naya current city banayenge ar ye step tab tak repeat karenge jab tak San Francisco na mil jaye ya saari cities visit na ho jayein. 4. Finally, smallest tentative distance waale path ko follow karke humein New York aur San Francisco ka shortest path mil jayega. Yaad rakhna ki shortest path map aur distances ke hisab se change hoga. Aur haan, Dijkstra's algorithm negative weights waale graphs pe kaam nahi karta.

instruction: Maan lo aap ek fraudulent financial transactions detect karne ka model bana rahe ho. Model evaluate karne ke liye kaunse metrics important honge?
output: Fraudulent transactions detect karne wale model ke liye ye metrics check karna zaroori hai: 1. Accuracy: Ye true positives aur true negatives ka proportion he. Ye janna zaroori hai ki kitne fraud cases sahi identify hue or kitne non-fraud cases sahi label hue. 2. Precision: Isse pata chalta hai ki predicted fraudulent transactions mein se actually kitne fraud the. High precision matlab false positives kam hain. 3. Recall: Isko sensitivity bhi kehte hain. Ye check karta hai ki total actual frauds mein se model ne kitne sahi pakde. High recall matlab false negatives kam hain. 4. F1 Score: Precision aur recall ka harmonic mean hai. Jab positive aur negative samples imbalanced hon ya false positives/negatives ki cost zyada ho, tab ye kaam aata hai. 5. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC): Ye metric batata hai ki model different decision thresholds par fraud aur non-fraud transactions ko kitne ache se distinguish kar pa raha ha. 6. Confusion Matrix: Ek table hai jo predicted vs actual values ko compare karta hai. Isse TP, TN, FP or FN ka clear picture mil jata hai. Overall, metrics aapke specific use case ar priority (false positives vs false negatives) ke hisaab se choose karo.

instruction: BST ka root diya hai, kisi bhi do nodes ke beech ka minimum absolute difference return karo.
output: Dekh, minimum absolute difference nikalne ke liye bas in-order traversal kar le aur adjacent nodes ko compare kar. Traversal ke time pe ek 'prev' node track kar (shuru mein null rakhna) aur uska value current node se compare kar. Agar difference ab tak ke minimum difference se kam hai, toh use update kar le. Python code ye raha: ``` class Solution: def getMinimumDifference(self, root: TreeNode) -> int: self.prev = None # previously visited node self.min_diff = float('inf') # initialize minimum difference as infinity def traverse(node): if node: traverse(node.left) if self.prev is not None: self.min_diff = min(self.min_diff, abs(node.val - self.prev.val)) self.prev = node traverse(node.right) traverse(root) return self.min_diff ``` Time complexity O(N) hai kyunki har node pe ek hi baar ja rahe hain.

instruction: Batao ki niche diya gaya code galat kyun hai. sum = 0 for i in range(len(num_list) sum = sum + num_list[i]
output: Ye code galat ha aur run nahi hoga kyunki isme do bade issues hain: 1. Syntax error: `for` loop ke end mein colon missing hai aur `range()` function ka closing bracket nahi lagaya. Isko theek karke aisa hona chahiye: ```for i in range(len(num_list)):``` 2. Indentation error: `for` loop ki body, matlab `sum = sum + num_list[i]` wali line, indented nahi hai. Isliye interpreter isko loop ka part nahi maanega. Is line ko indent karo: ```sum = sum + num_list[i]``` Toh basically, corrected code aisa dikhega: ``` sum = 0 for i in range(len(num_list)): sum = sum + num_list[i] ```

instruction: Identify karo ki (1, 2), (3, 4), (5, 10), aur (7, 6) points se kaunsa quadrilateral ban raha hai.
output: Ye points ek Trapezoid bana rahe hain. Maine aise conclude kiya: Pehle maine saare sides ke slopes calculate kiye. (1,2) aur (3,4) ka slope (4-2)/(3-1) = 1 aaya. (3,4) aur (5,10) ka slope (10-4)/(5-3) = 3. (5,10) aur (7,6) ka slope (6-10)/(7-5) = -2. Aur (7,6) aur (1,2) ka slope (2-6)/(1-7) = 2/3. Kyunki opposite sides ke slopes equal nah hain, toh ye parallelogram, rectangle ya square nahi ho sakta. Lekin, (1,2)-(3,4) aur (5,10)-(7,6) ke slopes ka product -2 hai, toh wo perpendicular hain jiska matlab wo sides parallel hain. Since quadrilateral mein ek pair parallel sides hai, isliye ye trapezoid hai.

instruction: Do alag types ke database management systems ko compare aur contrast karo. Relational aur Non-Relational database management systems
output: Dekho, Relational (RDBMS) aur non-relational (jise hum NoSQL kehte hain) do main types ke DBMS hote hain. Inke architecture, storage models aur data query karne ke tarike kaafi alag hote hain. Relational databases structured schema use karte hain, jahan data tables, rows aur columns mein organized hota aahe. Tables aapas mein keys ke through linked hote hain, toh SQL use karke multiple tables se data nikaalna easy ho jata hai. Isse data consistent rehta hai, toh financial software ya inventory management jaisi complex transactions ke liye ye best hai. Examples: MySQL, Oracle, MS SQL Server. Doosri taraf, non-relational databases ka koi fixed schema nahi hota, storage kaafi flexible hoti hai. Data key-value pairs, columns, documents ya graphs ki form mein save ho sakta hai. Toh jahan bahut saara unstructured ya semi-structured data ho—jaise social media, sensor data ya mobile apps—wahan ye kaam aata ah. Scalability bhi isme better milti hai. Examples: MongoDB, Cassandra, Redis. Short mein differences ye hain: - Structure: Relational mein structured schema hota hai, NoSQL mein flexible aur dynamic. - Storage: Relational tables use karta ha, NoSQL mein key-value, documents, columns aur graphs hote hain. - Querying: Relational mein SQL chalta hai, NoSQL mein alag-alag query languages ya APIs hote hain. - Scalability: NoSQL databases zyada scalable hote hain aur heavy data handle kar lete hain. Basically, choice is baat pe depend karti hai ki application ki requirement kya hai, data kaisa hai aur scalability kitni chahiye.

instruction: Ek cuboid ka surface area calculate karo jiska length 8 cm, width 4 cm aur height 9 cm hai.
output: Cuboid ka surface area nikalne ke liye hum saare six faces ke areas ko add karte hain. Since opposite faces equal hote hain, hum teen pairs ka area add kar sakte hain. Formula yeh hai: Surface area of cuboid = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh Yahan l length hai, w width hai aur h height aahe. Values put karne par: Surface area of cuboid = 2(8)(4) + 2(8)(9) + 2(4)(9) Ab isko solve karo: Surface area of cuboid = 64 + 144 + 72 = 280 square cm. Toh final surface area 280 square cm aayega.

instruction: Is task ka ek sample output banao: USA mein water resources par climate change ka kya impact hai, analyze karo.
output: Kaafi analysis ke baad yeh pata chala ki USA ke water resources par climate change ka kaafi bada impact pad raha hai. Global temperature badhne se hydrologic cycle disturb ho rahi hai, jiski wajah se water supply ki distribution, timing aur quantity badal gayi hai. Sabse pehla effect snow or ice ka pighalna hai. Glaciers aur snowpacks mein stored water kam ho raha hai, jo country ke kai hisson ke liye main storage system hain. Is wajah se kuch regions mein, khaaskar west mein, water shortage ho rahi hai kyunki summers mein snowmelt ka pani bahut zaroori hota hai. Temperature badhne se evaporation rates bhi badh rahe hain, jisse lakes, rivers aur reservoirs mein pani kam ho raha hai. Iska direct asar irrigation aur gharon mein use hone wale pani par padega. Precipitation patterns bhi change ho rahe hain. Kai jagah lambe drought pad rahe hain aur phir achanak bahut heavy rainfall hoti hai. Water managers ke liye planning karna mushkil ho gaya hai. Upar se, sea levels badhne ki wajah se coastal freshwater aquifers mein saltwater ghus raha hai. Isse coastal regions mein peene ke pani ki quality kharab ho rahi hai. Basically, climate change USA ke water resources ko buri tarah affect kar raha hai. Quantity aur quality dono gir rahi hain, to water managers ko jaldi adapt karne ki strategies banani padengi.

instruction: Ek string s aur integer k diya hai, har 2k characters mein se pehle k characters reverse karne hain. Agar k se kam characters bache hain, toh sab reverse kar do. Agar 2k se kam par k se zyada hain, toh pehle k reverse karo aur baaki ko original rehne do. Goal ye hai ki ek function design karo jo tax rate ke saath discounted price ke baad total amount calculate kare.
output: Python mein is string problem ke liye slicing aur string concatenation use kar sakte ho. Ye raha code: ```python def reverse_string(s, k): result = "" i = 0 while i < len(s): # reverse first k characters if i + k <= len(s): result += s[i:i+k][::-1] i += k # reverse remaining characters else: result += s[i:][::-1] break # leave next k characters as original if i + k <= len(s): result += s[i:i+k] i += k # include remaining characters as is else: result += s[i:] break return result ``` Aur total amount nikalne ke liye ye simple formula use karo: ```python total_amount = price - price * (tax_rate / 100) ``` Yahan `price` original amount ha aur `tax_rate` percentage hai.

instruction: Binary tree ka root diya gaya hai, tree ke diameter ki length return karo. Binary tree ka diameter kisi bhi do nodes ke beech ka longest path hota hai. Ye path root se pass ho bhi sakta hai aur nahi bhi. Do nodes ke beech path length ka matlab hai unke beech ke edges ka count.
output: Diameter nikalne ke liye do leaf nodes ke beech ka longest path find karna hoga. Sabse best tareeka hai tree ko recursively traverse karna aur har node par left aur right subtrees ki max depth calculate karna. In dono depths ko add karo (jo us node se passing longest path dikhayega) aur use current max diameter se compare karo. Python code ye raha: ```python class Solution: def diameterOfBinaryTree(self, root: TreeNode) -> int: self.diameter = 0 def depth(node): if not node: return 0 left = depth(node.left) right = depth(node.right) self.diameter = max(self.diameter, left + right) return 1 + max(left, right) depth(root) return self.diameter ``` Is solution mein `depth(node)` ek helper function hai jo subtree ki max depth return karta hai. Har node par hum left aur right depths ko add karke overall max diameter update karte hain. Last mein `depth(root)` call karke final result return kar diya. Done.

output: Is problem ko solve karne ke liye tum attendance record pe iterate karo aur absent aur late days ka count rakho. Do variables use kar lo—ek current consecutive late days ke liye aur ek max consecutive late days track karne ke liye. Agar 'A' mile, toh consecutive late count ko zero kar dena. End mein bas check karo ki absent days 2 se kam hain or max consecutive late days 3 se kam hain. Agar dono conditions true hain toh True return karo, nahi toh False. Python implementation ye raha: ```python def check_attendance(s: str) -> bool: absent_count = 0 max_consecutive_late_count = 0 consecutive_late_count = 0 for c in s: if c == 'A': absent_count += 1 consecutive_late_count = 0 elif c == 'L': consecutive_late_count += 1 max_consecutive_late_count = max(max_consecutive_late_count, consecutive_late_count) else: consecutive_late_count = 0 return absent_count < 2 and max_consecutive_late_count < 3 ``` Is function ko attendance record string pass karke call karo, ye True ya False return kar dega. Example ke liye: ```python >>> check_attendance("PPALLP") True >>> check_attendance("PPALLL") False ```

instruction: Climate change ka ocean ke rising sea levels pe kya effect hota hai, uspe ek report likho.
output: Climate change ek global problem hai jisse hamari planet ko bahut risks hain, including rising sea levels. 19th century ke end se sea level approx 8 inches badh chuka hai, aur iska aadha increase toh bas pichle do decades mein hua hai. Ye directly climate change aur greenhouse gases ki wajah se hone wali rapid warming se linked ah. Sea levels badhne ke do main reasons hain. Pehla hai thermal expansion—jab ocean atmosphere ki heat absorb karta he toh pani expand hota hai aur level badh jata hai. Dusra hai glaciers aur ice caps ka pighalna, jisse ocean mein pani zyada ho jata hai. Dono processes ab bahut fast ho rahe hain. Iska coastlines pe bahut bura asar pad raha ha. Low-lying areas mein thoda sa bhi level badhne se flooding, erosion aur groundwater mein saltwater ghusne lagta hai. Isse coastal communities aur infrastructure khatre mein hain aur millions of people ko apna ghar chhodna pad sakta hai. Marine ecosystems pe bhi iska asar hai. Water depth badalne se ocean species ki distribution aur abundance change ho jati ha, jisse biodiversity affect hoti hai. Coral reefs toh sabse zyada vulnerable hain kyunki unhe survive karne ke liye specific depth chahiye hoti ha. Conclusion ye aahe ki climate change sea levels ko significantly affect kar raha hai aur ye aage aur badhega. Isse millions displace honge aur ecosystems destroy honge. Humein abhi se greenhouse gas emissions kam karne honge taaki hum apni planet ko future generations ke liye bacha sakein.

instruction: For each pair of real numbers a b, define the operation ⋆ as (a ⋆ b) = (a + b)/(a - b). What is the value of ((1 ⋆ 2) ⋆ 3)?

instruction: Reverse engineer the following code and explain the logic of it. def find_smallest_multiple(n): x = n while True: if isDivisible(x, n): return x x += n
output: Ye code 1 function `find_smallest_multiple` define kar raha hai jo `n` naam ka ek integer parameter leta ha. Iska main kaam he `n` ka wo smallest multiple dhoondna jo 1 se lekar `n` tak ke saare integers se evenly divisible ho. Function shuru mein ek variable `x` ko `n` ke equal set karta hai. Phir ye ek `while True` infinite loop mein chala jata hai. Loop ke andar akk if statement hai jo `isDivisible()` function ko call karke check karta hai ki kya `x` saare numbers se divisible hai. Agar `x` divisible hai, toh function `x` ki value return kar deta hai. Agar nahi, toh `x` mein `n` add kiya jata hai ar loop phir se chalta ah. Ye tab tak chalta rehta hai jab tak koi aisi value na mil jaye jo criteria match kare. Basically, ye ek brute-force approach hai jahan multiples ko tab tak check kiya jata hai jab tak result na mil jaye.

instruction: Ek n-ary tree diya hai, uska maximum depth find karo. Maximum depth matlab root node se farthest leaf node tak ke longest path mein kitne nodes hain. Nary-Tree input serialization level order traversal mein hai, jahan har group of children null value se separated hai (examples dekh lo).
output: Iske liye recursive approach best rahegi. Pehle check karo ki root exist karta ah ya nahi; agar nahi toh depth 0 hai. Agar root hai, toh uske har child ke liye recursively max depth find karo. Phir jo maximum depth mile usme +1 add kar do (root node ke liye). Python code ye raha: ``` class Node: def __init__(self, val=None, children=None): self.val = val self.children = children def max_depth(root): if not root: return 0 children_depths = [max_depth(child) for child in root.children] return max(children_depths, default=0) + 1 ``` Bas is function mein root node pass karo or tumhe max depth mil jayegi.

instruction: Niche di gayi problem pe scientific method apply karo aur steps list karo. Can plants grow without sunlight?
output: Scientific method ek systematic approach hai jisme observation, question, hypothesis, experiment, data analysis aur conclusion aata hai. Is problem ke liye steps ye rahenge: 1. **Observation:** Hamein pata aahe ki plants generally grow karne ke liye sunlight use karte hain photosynthesis ke through, jisme light energy chemical energy mein convert hoti hai. 2. **Question:** Toh question ye hai ki kia plants bina sunlight ke grow kar sakte hain? 3. **Hypothesis:** Prediction karo, jaise ki "Plants bina sunlight ke grow naahi kar payenge kyunki photosynthesis ke liye light zaroori hai." 4. **Experiment:** Do identical plants lo, ek set ko sunlight mein rakho aur dusre set ko andhere mein. Kuch weeks ya months tak growth measure karo. 5. **Analysis of data:** Experiment ke baad data analyze karo. Dono sets ki growth compare karo aur dekho ki sunlight na hone se growth pe kya asar pada. 6. **Conclusion:** Results ke basis pe conclusion nikalo. Agar andhere wale plants grow nahi hue, toh hypothesis sahi thi. Agar growth same thi, toh hypothesis galat thi.

instruction: Diye gaye shape ka area meters mein kya hai? Rectangle jiski width 30mm aur height 50mm hai

Par yahan ek catch hai—measurements millimeters (mm) mein hain or question mein area meters (m) mein pucha gaya hai. Pehle measurements ko millimeters se meters mein convert karte hain: 30 mm = 30 / 1000 m = 0.03 m 50 mm = 50 / 1000 m = 0.05 m Ab area nikalne ke liye width aur height ko multiply karenge: Area = Width × Height Area = 0.03 m × 0.05 m Area = 0.0015 m² Conclusion: Is rectangle ka area 0.0015 square meters hai.

instruction: Batao ki modulo operator (%) ko use karke size 3 ke array par loop kaise chalate hain
output: Modulo operator (%) basically division ka remainder deta hai. Iska use karke hum size 3 ke array par loop chala sakte hain—bas loop ke index variable ka modulo array size (yaani 3) le lo, aur us result ko index ki tarah use karo. Isse jab index array size se bada hoga, toh woh wapas wrap-around hokar first element par aa jayega. Example dekho: ```python my_array = [10, 20, 30] array_size = len(my_array) index = 0 # loop 10 times for i in range(10): # Index variable i % array_size hai index = i % array_size # Calculated index se array element access karo print(my_array[index]) # Output: 10 20 30 10 20 30 10 20 30 10 ``` Is example mein, for loop 10 baar chal raha hai. Har iteration mein hum loop variable `i` ka modulo `array_size` le rahe hain, taaki index hamesha 0, 1, ya 2 hi rahe. Is wajah se array ke elements teen baar repeat honge aur fir cycle wapas start ho jayegi, total 10 outputs tak.

Yahan n total items hain aur k select karne wale. Toh calculation hogi: 15 choose 2 = 15! / (2! * (15-2)!) = 15 * 14 / 2 = 105 Toh total 105 ways hain co-presidents choose karne ke.

instruction: Do vectors diye hain, inka cosine similarity nikal lo. Vector1: [1.7, 6.2] Vector2: [3.4, 4.8]
output: Cosine similarity nikaalne ke liye ye formula use karna hoga: cosine_similarity = dot_product(Vector1, Vector2)/(magnitude(Vector1) * magnitude(Vector2)) Pehle dot product nikaalte hain: dot_product = (1.7 * 3.4) + (6.2 * 4.8) = 34.9 Ab dono vectors ka magnitude nikaalte hain: magnitude(Vector1) = sqrt(1.7^2 + 6.2^2) = 6.4817 magnitude(Vector2) = sqrt(3.4^2 + 4.8^2) = 5.8409 Ab final calculation karte hain: cosine_similarity = 34.9 / (6.4817 * 5.8409) = 0.9239 Toh Vector1 aur Vector2 ki cosine similarity 0.9239 ha.

instruction: Ek cylinder ka surface area calculate karo jiska radius 4.3 centimeters aur height 9.2 centimeters hai.
output: Cylinder ka surface area nikaalne ka formula ye hai: A = 2πr^2 + 2πrh Given values: r = 4.3 centimeters h = 9.2 centimeters Values put karte hain: A = 2π(4.3)^2 + 2π(4.3)(9.2) A = 2π(18.49) + 2π(39.56) A = 36.98π + 79.12π A ≈ 365.66 cm2 Answer approximately 365.66 square centimeter ha.

instruction: Ek positive integer n ke positive integer divisors ka product 729 hai. n ki value find karo.
output: Maan lo n ke d divisors hain aur d even he. Divisors pairs mein aate hain jinka product n hota hai, toh total product n^d/2 hoga. Example ke liye, agar n=12 hai, to divisors ka product (1*12)(2*6)(3*4) = 12^3 hoga. Agar d odd hai, toh (d-1)/2 pairs honge aur ek extra divisor sqrt(n) hoga. Toh product fir bhi n^[(d-1)/2] * n^1/2 = n^d/2 hi aayega. Example: n=16 ke liye product (1*16)(2*8)(4) = 16^(5/2). Summary ye hai ki product = n^d/2, jahan d divisors ka count hai. 729 ko 3^6 likh sakte hain, toh n^d/2 = 3^6. Iska matlab n^d = 3^12. Possible (n,d) pairs hain (3,12), (9,6), (27,4), (81,3) aur (729,2). Check karne par sirf (27,4) wale case mein d actually n ke divisors ka count hai, isliye n=27.

instruction: Ek dataset ke basis pe algorithm design karo. Dataset mein 10 variables aur 50 observations hain.

Feature selection: 10 variables hain, toh check karo kaunse predictive hain. Chi-squared ya ANOVA use karke complexity kam karo taaki overfitting na ho. 3. Model selection: Problem ke hisaab se model choose karo. Continuous variable hai toh regression, aur classification hai to Decision Tree, Random Forest ya SVM try karo. 4. Training: Data ko train aur test sets mein split karo, phir training data pe model fit karo. 5. Model evaluation: Accuracy, precision, recall ya MSE check karo. Reliable result ke liye cross-validation best rahega. 6. Fine-tuning: Agar performance low ah toh grid search ya random search se hyperparameters tune karo. 7. Final model: Best hyperparameters milne ke baad, pure dataset pe retrain karo aur predictions start karo. Bas ye steps follow karo aur tumhara algorithm ready hai.

instruction: Ek integer array 'nums' diya hai jisme 2n integers hain. Inko n pairs (a1, b1), (a2, b2)... mein group karo taaki sum of min(ai, bi) maximize ho jaye. Maximized sum return karo.
output: Dekho, minimums ka sum maximize karne ke liye humein pairs aise banane chahiye ki unka difference minimum ho. Sabse best tareeka ye hai ki array ko sort kar lo or consecutive elements ke pairs banao. Isse difference max 1 rahega kyunki array ki length even hai. Phir bas har pair ka minimum element add karte jao. Loop chalao aur sorted array se har second element uthao. Code ye raha: ```python def arrayPairSum(nums): nums.sort() return sum(nums[::2]) ``` Ye function array ko sort karta hai aur phir every other element ka sum return kar deta hai.

instruction: Cartesian coordinates use karke triangle ka area nikaalo. x1 = 0, y1 = 0, x2 = 7, y2 = 3, x3 = 11, y3 = 6
output: Shoelace formula use karte hain iska area nikalne ke liye. Simple polygon ka area nikalne ke liye yahi best hai. Given coordinates (x1, y1), (x2, y2), ar (x3, y3) ke liye formula hai: Area = 1/2 [| x1(y2 − y3) + x2(y3 − y1) + x3(y1 − y2) |] Values put karte hain: Area = 1/2 [| 0(3 − 6) + 7(6 − 0) + 11(0 − 3) |] Area = 1/2 [| 42 - 33 |] = 9/2 sq units Toh final area 4.5 sq units he.

instruction: Ek 3-dimensional vector banao jiske components x = 2, y = -1, z = 4 hon.
output: Dekh, 3D space mein vector basically teen real numbers ka ek ordered group hota aahe, x, y aur z components ke liye. Isko classically column matrix se dikha sakte hain. Given components ke hisab se, vector `v` jiske components x = 2, y = -1, aur z = 4 hain, use aise represent kar sakte hain: ``` v = [ 2 ] [-1 ] [ 4 ] ``` Baaki notations bhi use kar sakte ho, jaise pointed parentheses, angle brackets ya fir simple commas: * `v = <2, -1, 4>` * `v = (2, -1, 4)` * `v = 2i - j + 4k` (standard basis vectors i, j aur k use karke) Ye saare notations basically ek hi vector ko describe karte hain.

instruction: Ek right triangle ka hypotenuse nikalo jiske baaki do sides 5 cm aur 8 cm hain.
output: Right triangle mein hypotenuse nikalne ke liye Pythagorean theorem lagao—hypotenuse ka square baaki dono sides ke squares ke sum ke equal hota he. Agar sides 5 cm aur 8 cm hain, ta hypotenuse (c) aise niklega: c^2 = 5^2 + 8^2 c^2 = 25 + 64 c^2 = 89 c = √89 c ≈ 9.43 cm Toh basically, hypotenuse ki length approximately 9.43 cm hogi.

instruction: In dono stocks ki total value calculate karo. Apple stock: 1,000 shares @ $200 per share Google stock: 500 shares @ $100 per share

instruction: Us line ki equation nikalo jo x+y+z=5 aur y+z=1 planes se pass hoti hai.
output: Do planes ke intersection se line ki equation nikalne ke liye pehle intersection dhundna padega. Hamare paas x+y+z=5 aur y+z=1 hai, toh second equation ko first se subtract kar do: x+y+z - (y+z) = 5-1. Isse x=4 aa jayega. Ab ye x ki value kisi bhi plane equation mein dalo toh y+z=1 milega. Matlab intersection wali line x=4, y+z=1 form mein aahe. Isko parametric aise likh sakte hain: x = 4 y = t z = 1 - t Jahan t parameter hai. Toh parametric equation ho gayi: x = 4 y = t z = 1 - t. Aur iski equivalent vector equation aise hogi: r = <4,0,1> + t<0,1,-1>

instruction: Is claim ko investigate karo: Roman Empire technology ke maamle mein sabse advanced tha.
input: The Roman Empire was the most advanced in terms of technology.
output: Dekho, 'advanced' aur 'technology' ka matlab alag-alag ho sakta hai, toh is claim ko properly check karne se pehle context zaroori hai. Par overall scene ye hai: Roman Empire apne time ke hisab se engineering aur construction technology mein kaafi aage tha. Roman engineers roads, aqueducts, bridges aur monumental buildings banane mein expert the. Unhone public baths, fountains aur amphitheaters jaise bade projects banaye. Concrete use karne ki wajah se unke structures pehle waalon se zyada bade aur durable the. Rome ka Colosseum iska best example hai. Construction ke alaava, hydraulics mein bhi unka haath saaf tha. Unhone water supply aur sanitation ke liye complex aqueducts aur underground sewers banaye the jo clean water door tak le ja sakte the aur waste ko city se bahar nikal sakte the. Metallurgy, glassmaking aur ceramics mein bhi wo kaafi skilled the, daily use ke tools aur glassware badhiya banate the. Par haan, baaki civilizations bhi peeche nah thi. Jaise Han Dynasty (China) ne economics, science, math aur astronomy mein kaafi progress ki thi. Toh basically, 'advanced' hona interpretation pe depend karta hai. Romans kuch areas mein top pe the, par bina clear definition ke ye kehna mushkil hai ki wo overall sabse advanced the.

instruction: In facts ko use karke Einstein ki ek biography likho. Name: Albert Einstein Born: March 14, 1879 Died: April 18, 1955 Known for: Theory of relativity Achievements: Nobel Prize in Physics 1921
output: Albert Einstein ek bahut bade physicist the, jo mainly apni theory of relativity ke liye jaane jaate hain. Unka janam 14 March, 1879 ko Ulm, Württemberg, Germany mein hua tha. Shuruat mein unhone ek Catholic elementary school mein padhai ki, par unhe religion aur teachers ka authoritative nature pasand nahi aaya. Baad mein unhone Zurich ke Swiss Federal Polytechnic se apni degree 1900 mein complete ki. Einstein ki sabse badi achievements theoretical physics mein thi, jahan unhone general relativity ki theory di, jo modern physics ke do main pillars mein se ek hai. Saath hi statistical mechanics aur quantum theory mein bhi unka bada contribution raha, jisne aage chalkar kai important developments ki foundation rakhi. 1921 mein, Einstein ko photoelectric effect ki discovery ke liye Nobel Prize in Physics mila, jisne quantum mechanics ke development ka raasta saaf kiya. Iske alawa unhe kai academic institutions se awards aur honors mile, aur unka naam 'genius' ka synonym ban gaya. Einstein 18 April, 1955 ko 76 saal ki age mein expire huye, lekin science community mein wo end tak active rahe. Unka kaam aur contributions aaj bhi scientists ko inspire karte hain, aur unka naam extraordinary intellect aur creativity ki pehchaan ban chuka hai.

instruction: Binary tree ke root se har node ka tilt sum return karo. Ek tree node ka tilt, left subtree node values ke sum aur right subtree node values ke sum ke beech ka absolute difference hota hai. Agar kisi node ka left child nahi hai, toh left subtree ka sum 0 maana jayega. Same rule right child ke liye bhi apply hota hai.
output: Is problem ko solve karne ke liye aap ek recursive function bana sakte ho jo tree ko traverse kare aur har node ka tilt calculate kare. Ye algorithm follow karo: 1. Ek "tiltSum" variable lo aur use 0 set karo. 2. "calculateTilt" naam ka ek recursive function likho jo node ko as an argument le. 3. Function ke andar check karo agar node null hai, ta 0 return karo. 4. Left aur right subtree ke liye calculateTilt ko recursively call karo. 5. Current node ka tilt nikaalo (left subtree sum aur right subtree sum ka absolute difference). 6. Is tilt value ko "tiltSum" variable mein add karo. 7. Left sum, right sum aur current node ki value ka total return karo. 8. Root node ke saath calculateTilt function ko call karo. 9. Finally, "tiltSum" ki value return kar do. Ye raha Python code jo is algorithm ko implement karta hai: ``` class TreeNode: def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None): self.val = val self.left = left self.right = right class Solution: def findTilt(self, root: TreeNode) -> int: tiltSum = 0 def calculateTilt(node): nonlocal tiltSum if not node: return 0 leftSum = calculateTilt(node.left) rightSum = calculateTilt(node.right) tilt = abs(leftSum - rightSum) tiltSum += tilt return leftSum + rightSum + node.val calculateTilt(root) return tiltSum ``` Note: Is code mein assume kiya gaya hai ki TreeNode class mein "val" attribute hai aur "left" aur "right" attributes subtrees ko point karte hain.

instruction: Socho ki tum ek tour guide ho aur Statue of Liberty ke baare mein kuch information do.
output: Ek virtual tour guide ban kar main aapko US ke sabse iconic landmarks mein se ek—Statue of Liberty ke baare mein batata hoon. Statue of Liberty New York Harbor ke Liberty Island par hai. France ne ise 1886 mein US ko gift kiya tha, taaki American Declaration of Independence ke 100 saal poore hone ka jashn manaya ja sake aur dono countries ki gehri dosti dikhayi ja sake. Isse French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi ne design kiya tha. Ye akk bahut badi neoclassical sculpture ah jiski height base se torch tak 151 feet 1 inch hai. Agar pedestal ko bhi mila lein, toh total height 305 feet 6 inches ho jati he. Ye copper se bani hai aur shuru mein dull brown color ki thi, par time ke saath oxidize hokar ab greenish-blue dikhti hai. Ye statue Libertas ki ah, jo freedom ki Roman goddess hain. Right hand mein unhone akk torch pakdi hui hai jo enlightenment ka symbol hai, aur left hand mein 1 tablet hai jispe American Declaration of Independence ki date, July 4, 1776, likhi hai. Unke pairon ke paas ek tooti hui chain hai jo oppression ke khatam hone ko dikhati hai. Visitors 354 steps chadh kar pedestal tak ja sakte hain jahan se harbor aur city skyline ka amazing view dikhta hai. Statue of Liberty sirf ek art piece nahi he, balki poori duniya ke liye freedom, democracy aur hope ka symbol hai.

instruction: Ek medical condition di gayi hai. Uska 3-5 sentences mein description likho: Moyamoya Syndrome
output: Moyamoya syndrome ek rare aur progressive cerebrovascular disorder hai, jisme internal carotid arteries aur unki main branches narrow ya block ho jati hain, jis se brain mein blood flow kam ho jata hai. Iski wajah se transient ischemic attacks, strokes, seizures aur baaki neurological symptoms aa sakte hain. Ye condition adults ke mukable bachon mein zyada common hai, par kisi bhi age group ke person ko ho sakti hai. Iska naam Moyamoya hai, jiska Japanese mein matlab 'puff of smoke' hota aahe, kyunki angiogram par blockage ko compensate karne ke liye jo tiny vessels banti hain, wo dhuein ke badal jaisi dikhti hain. Iska treatment usually surgical procedures se hota hai taaki brain ke affected areas mein blood flow wapas start ho sake.
